content: ECIL procures materials and components on a regular basis from suppliers spread throughout the country & recognizes outsourcing as one of the strategic tools to achieve cost benefits and also complement the strengths of private sector to build a strong industrial base. To facilitate the same, ECIL has well established procedures to carry out purchase, sub-contract and works contract activities as per the respective manuals approved by the Competent Authority. These manuals also follow the guidelines issued by CVC from time to time. ECIL carries out Procurement through following modes like E-Procurement Portal, GeM Portal etc., as per the Government guidelines and also publishes the tenders on the Central Public Procurement Portal (CPPP) for wide reach & publicity. ECIL is backed by a strong supplier-base which is continually updated. New suppliers and traders (only those who are sole/authorized representatives of OEMs), who would give ECIL competitive inputs, are being added to the list of existing suppliers on regular basis. content: Electronics Corporation of India Limited (ECIL) a Schedule-A Central Public Sector Enterprise (CPSE) was incorporated on 11th April, 1967 under the administrative control of Department of Atomic Energy (DAE) with an objective to generate strong indigenous capabilities in the field of professional grade electronics. The Vision, Mission, Objectives of ECIL are defined to strengthen the capabilities. The initial accent was on total Self Reliance with years of expertise, ECIL today serves various government commercial sectors and has been instrumental in leading the IT and Electronics revolution in India and is Contributing to Atmanirbhar Bharat since inception. Over the years, ECIL pioneered the development of various complex electronics products without any external technological help and scored several firsts in these fields. Though the initial thrust was on meeting the Control Instrumentation requirements of the Nuclear Power Program, the expanded scope of self-reliance pursued by ECIL enabled the company to Design, Develop, Manufacture various products and provide Life Cycle Support to cater to the needs of Defence, Civil Aviation, Information Broadcasting, Telecommunications, Insurance, Banking, Police, and Para-Military Forces, Oil Gas, Power, Space Education, Health, Agriculture, Steel and Coal sectors and various user departments in the Government domain. ECIL thus evolved as a multi-product company serving multiple sectors of Indian economy with emphasis on import of country substitution and development of products & services that are of economic and strategic significance to the country. ECIL believes in creating sustained value through effective utilisation of resources and created infrastructure to meet the future needs. Our Integrated business model helps us to be self sufficient culminating into strategic projects that contribute towards the countries goals of becoming Atmanirbhar by regularly engaging with our esteemed customers. In a significant milestone for the Electronics Corporation of India Limited (ECIL), the Government of India has officially conferred the company with the prestigious Miniratna (Category-I) Status. This recognition, granted by the Department of Atomic Energy (DAE) under the PMO, serves as a testament to ECIL’s consistent financial performance, operational excellence, and adherence to rigorous eligibility criteria. ECIL's elevation to Miniratna Category-I status grants it enhanced financial and operational autonomy, reinforcing its leadership in strategic electronics and its commitment to a self-reliant Atmanirbhar Bharat, while simultaneously bolstering its corporate reputation and market value within the national strategic sector. Over Five Decades of service to the Nation in the field of Strategic Electronics making India Self-reliant in overcoming technology denial in niche areas for strategic applications. ECIL has spearheaded the development of Indigenous electronics in the country and is proud to have introduced many firsts, ranging from miniature components to complex systems encompassing Instrumentation, Communication and Digital Computer etc. ECIL pioneered the development of various complex electronic products without any external technological help and scored several firsts in these fields Journey of Innovations continues with the development of New Technologies to empower the Nation in the true spirit of Atmanirbhar Bharat in the recent past like:

content: The genesis of Electronics Corporation of India Limited (ECIL) can be traced back to the work undertaken at the Electronics Production Division, Reactor Controls Division, and Computers Group of the Atomic Energy Establishment, Trombay (AEET) since its inception. By the late 1960s, AEET (renamed as Bhabha Atomic Research Centre- BARC) had a significant electronic group, wherein research and development were carried out on silicon crystal, compound semiconductors, ceramics, transistors, diodes, carbon resistors, metal-film resistors, and tantalum capacitors. Additionally, analog and digital computer modules were manufactured and successfully tested. Recognizing the nascent state of the electronics industry in India and its anticipated future requirements, a national committee for electronics was formed in 1963, with Dr. Homi J. Bhabha as its Chairman along with Dr. Vikram Sarabhai, Dr. Bhagavantham and Dr. A. S. Rao, representatives of the Department of Defence and communications and other user departments as the members of this committee. The Committee recommended to establish an independent entity dedicated to Nuclear Electronic Instruments/systems and Electronic Components. The Committee prepared a comprehensive report covering all major areas of electronics including computers, communications, Components and consumer electronics. The objective was clearly on achieving self-reliance in electronics so as to put India on par with the developed countries, modernize Indian industry through new technology and open up vast employment opportunities for Indian scientists and engineers. Against this backdrop, Electronics Corporation of India Ltd (ECIL) a Schedule- "A" CPSE under the Department of Atomic Energy (DAE) was established in April 1967 with the main objective of meeting the requirements of nuclear electronic instruments & systems, nuclear detectors & monitoring systems for Nuclear Power Programme of the country with Dr. AS. Rao as founder Managing Director and Dr. Vikram Sarabhai as Chairman. The first Board of Directors meeting took place in Mumbai, led by Founder Chairman Dr. Vikram Sarabhai and Founder Managing Director Dr. A.S. Rao, alongside other distinguished stalwarts. The activities were started from Sanath Nagar Industrial Estate, Sanath Nagar, Hyderabad. Any write up on the institutes of Department of Atomic Energy (DAE) such as ECIL would be incomplete without a word on Dr. Bhabha. Dr. Homi J. Bhabha is considered as the Father of India's Atomic Energy Programme. Every institution of DAE is a translation of Dr. Bhabha's magnificent vision of enriching the country with talent and technology into reality. Modern India owes a great deal to him for the foundation he laid for science and technology and the avenues he created for bright young scientists and engineers to make their invaluable contributions to the nation. It was Dr. Bhabha, who realized the need to establish a strong indigenous base for professional grade electronic equipment in the country. The talent Dr. Bhabha and his associates nurtured has left a lasting legacy. It is matter of great pride to ECIL that Dr. Bhabha personally selected the site where the company would be located. Dr. Vikram Sarabhai (1919-1971) "To play a meaningful role nationally, and in the community of nations, we must be second to none in the application of advanced technologies to the real problems of man and society" ... Dr. Vikram Sarabhai Dr. Vikram Sarabhai combined the flair for research with the acumen of a businessman. He had no hesitation in pioneering a commercial production unit that would bring to the country the benefits and fruits of the R&D carried out over the years in the field of electronics at Bhabha Atomic Research Centre (BARC). Electronics Corporation of India Limited was established under Department of Atomic Energy on 11th April 1967 with Dr. Vikram Sarabhai as Chairman. ECIL and its growth were dear to Dr. Vikram Sarabhai and amidst other important work he always devoted considerable time for the Corporation all through his tenure from 1967 to 1971. ECIL fondly remembered Dr. Vikram Sarabhai’s innovative leadership and commitment for Self-Reliance in electronics on his 100th Birth Anniversary during 2018-19. "Let us work up the embers of national pride latent in all of us and build up our morale so that we can confidently aim high and achieve greater goals"... Dr. A.S.Rao Proudly, no other founder of any Indian Public Sector Enterprise is so completely identified with Electronics Corporation of India Limited (ECIL). For many, even now, Dr. A.S.Rao is ECIL and vice versa. The respect for him in the company borders the worship. Dr. Rao spent many years under the dynamic leadership of Dr. Homi J Bhabha. At ECIL, Dr. Rao religiously implemented the motto of self reliance. He led ECIL with remarkable motivation and missionary zeal for more than a decade. During his tenure every critical electronic product required for the nation was made by ECIL. ECIL Permanent Office buildings at Moulali, Hyderabad are an architectural masterpiece in itself and the construction works have commenced with the help of renowned architect Kamal Mangaldas. The buildings were characterized by flexible lay outs with de-mountable partitions. They were steel and glass constructions and certainly were a novelty in those days. Dr. Vikram Sarabhai has requested the architect to design the buildings so as to eliminate the need for mechanical air conditioning devices. To minimise heat input, shade was provided by a large overhanging roof that consisted of a slatted pergola and thin membrane of water to reflect the sunlight back into the sky. This was the first ever construction of a pergola in Hyderabad. The First Production Divisions were Nuclear Allied Instruments Division (NID), Resistors and Capacitors Division (RCD), the Semiconductors Division (SMD), the Power Reactor Instruments Division (PRID) and the Microwave Division (MWD). Ever since its formation, ECIL has had a remarkable growth in size, turnover, product range and the number of persons employed despite being the first ever Undertaking of its kind in the field, based entirely on indigenous know-how, at a time when it was the rule to have foreign collaboration for such high technology enterprises. Between the period 1967 to 1977 ECIL achieved an annual Growth rate of nearly 80%. The company attained break-even operations within three years, making a maiden profit of Rs. 1.4 million during 1970-71, the fourth year of operation. ECIL has spearheaded the development of Indigenous electronics in the country by overcoming technology denial in niche areas for strategical applications and is proud to have introduced many firsts, ranging from miniature components to complex systems encompassing Instrumentation, Communication and Digital Computer. Prominent among the firsts are: ECIL has since expanded and diversified into a multi-product, multi-disciplinary and multi-technology organisation providing cutting-edge technology solutions of national importance in Defence, Aerospace, Security, IT & e-Governance sectors besides meeting the core mandate of DAE requirements in nuclear sector. Instruments Group: of ECIL had developed 50 MH all solid-state oscilloscope, Ultrasonic flaw detectors for non-destructive testing of axles by railways. Using the know-how developed by CEERI, successfully developed 1500 numbers of E-Type excitation control systems required for the railways for their WDM Locos for excitation control of traction generator, dynamic braking regulation, speed control of the diesel engine, transition control, locomotive speed indication and battery charging. For Defence, Instruments Group supplied sound ranging systems for the Army to detect enemy gun artillery, portable life boat radio station and auto alarm receiver for sailors and automatic data handling system for Airforce, all of which meet the exact requirements of extreme temperatures and humidity. Communication Group: Communication was an important activity of ECIL from the early stage of its operations. One of the major activities was the design and manufacture of troposcatter communication antenna of the parabolic reflector and bill board type required by the Ministry of Defence for national border security. In collaboration with Space Applications Centre, ECIL understood the detailed working of the reflection microwave transmission system. More than 200 troposcatter antenna structures have been designed, manufactured, supplied and commissioned by ECIL played a major and memorable part in the Satellite Instruction Television Experiment for which the company supplied over 2500 community TV receivers with front-end converters and chicken-mesh parabolic antenna for direction reception of TV signals via satellite. Computer Group: Since its formation, Computer has been one of the thrust areas of ECIL. The indigenous computer development programme was pursued initially at TIFR, Indian Statistical Institute, BARC and the Jadavpur University, Calcutta and one model of AC20 analog computers was introduced in the market. Further to the growth of Digital Computers, R and D efforts were carried out in the digital technology and successful prototype of a 12-bit computer in 1969 was developed as a first major milestone. Dr. Sarabhai recognised immediately the significant role computers were going to play in various spheres of activity including research and wanted ECIL to expand the scope of activity, TDC-12 with its solid-state technology was produced at ECIL and by 1971, around 20 systems were supplied to various users like Seismic Station at Gauribidanur for round the clock monitoring of seismic data pertaining to earthquakes of nuclear explosions. The Electronics Commission came into existence in 1971, with Prof. MGK Menon as Chairman, decided to assist ECIL in carrying out R and D work, that would make India self-sufficient in small, mini, medium and large computers. Using this assistance, ECIL brought out TDC-312 , a third generation version of TDC-12 with enhanced software and TDC-316 , a highly versatile 16-bit computer system suitable for scientific, commercial and real-time applications. TDC-316 had fairly long life cycle and was in use from 1973 and 1985 in various forms. Fourth generation computer of India micro 78 was introduced in 1977 using large scale integrated circuits and first medium large computer System 332 with 32-bit word length was introduced in 1979. In the area of software, ECIL was the first to come out with a general purpose operating system, one of the most complex systems to be developed and compilers for FORTRAN and COBOL, the standard programming languages for scientific and business applications. These developments were pioneering efforts and their successful delivery, despite scepticism from many corners, to hundreds of customers in the country, augured well for building confidence in the strategically, important software industry in the country. In the complex real time area, ECIL had many notable achievements. A dual processor TDC316 system was supplied to Fast Breeder Test Reactor at Kalpakkam for monitoring various parameters. Highly advanced message switching systems were supplied to the Army and the Air Force. A sophisticated all weather proof ruggedized air defence system has been supplied to the Defence Services for monitoring the countries air space. Consumer Electronics Group: ECIL had also participated in SITE programme with the objective of making possible intercontinental reception and TV reception available to remote rural pockets. ECIL produced TV receivers of special design with front end converters that can receive transmission directly from the satellite without the aid of any other ground installation. Besides the major activities described so far in the areas of control, instrumentation, communication, computer and consumer electronics, ECIL also had a Components Division that was engaged in the supply of professional grade components such as tantalum capacitors, metal film resistors and nickel cadmium batteries. ECIL further ventured into other domains of Aerospace, Defence, Homeland Security, e-Governance by following the Self-Reliance as basic Philosophy and contributing to the nation building. title: Corporate Governance | ECIL | DAE | India
content: ECIL is committed to meet highest standards of Corporate Governance by ensuring compliances to regulatory laws, diligently following laid down procedures and maintaining transparency in business operations. ECIL upholds highest standards of business ethics in all operations and decision-making processes while ensuing customer Satisfaction, Financial Prudence and retaining core values in all our operations. The Company continues to take several measures to enhance the openness and transparency of all its operations, in line with Govt. guidelines. ECIL is a ‘Government Company’ in terms of the provisions of Sec 2(45) of the Companies Act, 2013, as the entire paid-up capital of the company is held by Central Government, through the President of India, including the nominees. The Board of ECIL comprises of well-experienced personnel as its directors and has appropriate mix of Functional Directors including C&MD, Government Nominee Directors, part-time Official Directors and part-time non-Official (Independent) Directors. The Board meets at regular intervals and is responsible for the proper direction and management of the Company. In alignment with the Guidelines on Corporate Governance for Central Public Sector Enterprises (2010) mandated by Department of Public Enterprises (DPE), ECIL Board has established a formal Code of Conduct for all Board Members and Senior Management. To ensure continuous adherence, all Board Members and Senior Management Personnel provide a formal affirmation of compliance with this Code at the commencement of each financial year. CODE OF BUSINESS CONDUCT AND ETHICS FOR BOARD MEMBERS AND SENIOR MANAGEMENT (pdf /34.62 KiB). In order to comply with the requirements under the Companies Act, 2013, the Corporate Governance Guidelines of DPE and the Board directives, the following Board level sub-committees are constituted: Audit Committee (pdf / 623.53 KiB) Corporate Social Responsibility Committee (pdf / 621.63 KiB) Remuneration Committee (pdf / 622.26 KiB) Contract Negotiation Committee (pdf / 622.80 KiB) Board of Directors have approved policy on training of the Directors in compliance with Corporate Governance Guidelines issued by DPE. On joining of a new Director, a welcome letter by Chairman & Managing Director together with business profile of the Company is being sent to the newly appointed Director. The management of the Company familiarizes the newly appointed Directors about the company, its products, business processes, governance, internal controls, regulations and with other relevant important information concerning the Company. Based on the convenience of the Director a visit to factory and other places of operation is also being arranged to make the new Director familiar with the operations, processes of the Company. The Board of Directors of the Company consists of CMD, Functional Directors and part-time Directors from DAE, Ministry of Defence, other Government organizations/ Departments and other CPSEs or practicing professionals. The Directors are having requisite knowledge on matters relating to functioning of the Company. Directors are also encouraged for attending important training programmes on the subjects of Corporate Governance, Board related practices and orientation programmes etc, conducted by various institutes of repute, Government Institutions and DPE. Policy on Training of Directors (pdf / 40.38 KiB) With a view to establish a mechanism for the employees to report to the Management about their concerns regarding unethical behavior and the cases of actual or suspected fraud, violation of Company’s general guidelines on Conduct and Ethics, the Company implemented the Whistle Blower Policy. The Policy ensures that adequate safeguards are provided to the genuine Whistle Blower against victimization. In terms of the policy any aggrieved employee can directly approach Chairman of Audit Committee. Whistle Blower Policy (pdf / 231.19 KiB) The Company has complied with the applicable Guidelines on Corporate Governance for CPSEs issued by the Department of Public Enterprises, Government of India. The Company is also submitting quarterly compliance report regularly to the Department of Public Enterprises and to the Department of Atomic Energy, Government of India.

title: Manufacturing Units & Offices | ECIL | DAE | India
content: ECIL, established in 1967 under the Department of Atomic Energy had the primary objective of productionising the products developed at BARC, Mumbai in order to support the Country’s Nuclear Power and other Atomic Energy Programmes. Concurrently, it has endeavored to create a strong indigenous / production base in the Country for professional grade electronics spanning from small passive components to large and complex computer based systems. Initial manufacturing activities commenced at the Sanath Nagar Industrial Estate, followed by the establishment of the main factory near Moula Ali, Hyderabad. Further ECIL has established the EVM Manufacturing & Services Division (EMSD) Facility at Cherlapalli Industrial Area specializing in the mass production of strategic electronic systems and high-density PCB assemblies. Located on a 55-acre campus with 10,000 sq. meters of advanced facilities, EMSD integrates automation, precision assembly, and testing to deliver secure, high-quality, and time-bound manufacturing. In order to meet the manufacturing requirements of Black & White Televisions, ECIL has established Tirupati Unit in the year 1984. The facility was further used to provide services to Register General of India (RGI) and for manufacturing and supply of Power Packs for EMVs & VVPAT machines etc., to ECI and various SECs of different states for Election requirements. The Company has thus evolved over the years as a multi-product Company serving multiple sectors of Indian economy with emphasis on Import Substitution and development of products and services that are of economic and strategic importance to the Country spanning the strategic sectors of Atomic Energy, Defence, Aerospace, Security, IT & e-Governance.

Various types of Radiation Detectors were supplied to Indian nuclear power plants and facilities to ensure the safe and secure operation. These detectors include in-core and ex-core neutron detectors for Reactor start-up, control, protection, failed fuel detection, and health physics applications. Detectors for neutron, gamma, and beta radiation undergo necessary tests and are qualified to meet seismic, vibration, and environmental specifications in accordance with the relevant standards for nuclear power plants and establishments. The product range and compliance practices tailored to the specific materials we work with. ECIL has established infrastructure and state-of-the-art facilities to support design, prototyping, full-scale in-house manufacturing, and characterization. Our specialized facilities include nuclear material plating, 10 BF 3 gas generation & purification, He-3 leak detection systems, Cesium Iodide/Sodium Iodide crystal growth laboratory, photo detector characterisation facility, precision machining, NABL accredited radiological calibration facilities, mineral-insulated cable assemblies. Boron coated proportional counters are used for thermal neutron detection. These detectors use metallic Boron powder enriched in isotope 10 B for the purpose of detection of thermal neutrons. The 10 B atoms have high thermal neutron interaction cross-section through reaction. B 10 + 0 1 n → 3 7 Li 3 + 2 4 He 2 + 2.31 MeV ECIL make B¹⁰ coated proportional counters have robust design. High pure ceramic to metal seals, are used for the purpose of isolation of electrodes. The detectors are hermetic sealed and helium leak tested to a level of < 1 × 10⁻⁹ std cc/sec. This ensures long life of the B¹⁰ counters. The detectors are integrated with radiation resistant super screenedcable having low attenuation to transmit signal to longer distances. These detectors are also terminated with mineral insulated cable when they need to be operated in high temperature environment. These detectors are usually manufactured with sensitivity 4cps/nv (nominal); The sensitivity depends on parameters like sensitive length and area of detector, enrichment of 10 B and in fact the integrated electronics. ECIL make 10 B coated neutron detectors are usually tested with standard proportional counting system to determine the sensitivity. Custom made designs could be done to have sensitivity between 1 to 20 cps/nv These detectors could operate in low neutron flux with high gamma background. These detectors have 10 to 15% loss in sensitivity when operated in gamma flux of 10³ R/hr. There is no appreciable change in the integral discriminator bias characteristics up to a background gamma of 1 R/hr for 20 cps/nv detectors and 100 R/hr for 4 cps/nv detectors The length of plateau depends on slope of gas multiplication curve and thus the fill pressure and geometry of detector. Plateau length of usually 100V with very good slope is achieved. The insulation resistance of these detectors is usually ≥ 1 Tera Ohm at room temperature and Relative Humidity < 60%. Mineral Insulated Cablesterminated detectors have good insulation even in high humidity environments. The detectors nominal rated continuous operating temperature is 60°C.For specially made high temperature 10 B coated proportional counters, the maximum operating temperature is 150°C. Customization of dimension, sensitivity, body material etc. is possible. The estimated life of these detectors is about cumulative neutron fluence rate of 10 18 nvt to show any appreciable degradation in the counter performance. The voltage region in which there is not much variation in detection sensitivity. Nominal operation voltage is 750 to 850 Volts DC. The amplification gain and discriminator setting of associated electronics may show influence on operating region. These detectors are qualified for nuclear application and regularly used for Neutron flux monitoring during reactor physical and normal start-up. These are used for in-core/ ex-core neutron flux measurement in the presence of high gamma field at NPPs. 10 BF 3 gas-filled detectors are operated in the proportional region, in which output variation is proportional to the incident neutron flux. These detectors are filled with pure 10 BF 3 gas below atmospheric pressure. The gas acts as both the sensitive and ionizing medium. 10 B atoms in the gas have a thermal neutron capture cross section of ≈3800 barns The more probable interaction is: 10 B + 0 1 n → 3 7 Li 3 + 2 4 He 2 + 2.31 MeV Because of high cross-section of neutron interaction and good charge generation per event, these detectors are preferred to be used as high sensitive detectors. Cathode is usually made of stainless steel of grade SS304L and Anode is made of thin Tungsten wire. For electrical isolation, high pure ceramic-to-metal seals are used. The quality of detector is estimated using pulse height analyzer. The full width at half maxima (FWHM) for ECIL make detectors is <30%(nominal). Plateau length is the range of high voltage over which count rate doesn’t vary much.Plateau length will be ≥300V. Operating voltage is around 1800V when operated with standard proportional counting system. It is defined as counts per second at operating voltage per incident neutron flux Theoretical expression for sensitivity is, S = NV / σ where ‘N’ is number of 10 B nuclei per unit volume. V is sensitive volume of detector ³He neutron detectors are meant for measurement of low thermal neutron flux. Helium-3 gas is doped with stopping power inert gas for better charge collection. These detectors work on the principle of thermal neutron capture reaction ³He(n,p) The detectors are made using stainless steel SS304L grade metal walls and ceramic metal seals with high insulation resistance. Detectors are usually terminated with HN connector. All detectors are Helium leak tested to a level of <1 × 10⁻⁹ std. cc/sec before gas filling. He-3 gas is doped with high stopping power gas for better charge collection. Sensitivity is established using standard reference detector calibrated using gold foil irradiation method. Boron-10 coated ion chambers are used for measuring neutron flux in the intermediate and power range of reactor operation. These chambers work on same principle as of 10 B coated proportional counters where in thermal neutron capture interaction happens. This detector operates on principle of collection of charge generated during primary ionization due to interaction of sensitive medium with neutrons. Signal is obtained as current output corresponding to averaged neutron flux level. The body of the detector is made with 19500 grade high pure Aluminum. Boron enriched in 10 B is used as sensitive medium. The detector is usually integrated with tri-axial Mineral(MgO) insulated cable, terminated with tri axial connector. Detector could also be terminated with connectors instead of mineral insulated cable integrated. The detectors are tested for voltage-current characteristics at different neutron flux levels. Sensitivity is established using standard reference detector calibrated using gold foil irradiation method. ECIL make detectors are tested for Linearity over neutron flux range of 100 nV to 10⁷ nV to simulate in-situ site testing. * Can be supplied without MI cable with two nos. of HN receptacles mounted on the detector ECIL make Miniature Neutron detector designed for Intermediate Range Monitor consists of Mineral Insulated Cable of low capacitance integrated to the detector. This is used for monitoring the in-core neutron flux during the intermediate range in Boiling Water Reactors. The miniature fission detectors are designed with an electrode gap of 0.25mm for monitoring in-core neutron flux in Boiling Water Reactors (BWR) during Power Range. These detectors operate at very low voltage even in full power conditions. The detector along with integral Mineral Insulated cable has been hydro-tested for 150 Kg/cm² pressure. These fission detectors are designed for operating in source range neutron flux in Boiling Water Reactors (BWR). These detectors operate at very low voltage. The detector along with integral Mineral Insulated cable has been hydro-tested for 150 Kg/cm² pressure. The detector is a cylindrical chamber with integral tri-axial mineral insulated cables with neutron sensing material coated on electrodes. Thesse detectors monitor neutron flux with high gamma field background and high temperature of 500 0 C. These are specially developed for FBRs. The detectors are made of Inconel-600 material. Self-Powered Neutron Detectors (SPNDs) are being manufactured to meet the requirement of in-core Neutron Flux in Nuclear Power Reactors. Emitter is a Neutron sensitive material in the detector which emits charged/ionizing radiation when a Neutron interacts with it. The gap between emitter and collector is very less and thus no potential is required to collect the charged radiation/particles. A potential difference is created due to the transfer of this charge to the collector electrode thus leading to a current flow between emitter and current which is the output signal of SPND. The signal communication cable for SPND is usually a Mineral Insulated cable with either single or double conductors. The component in the output due to parasitic signals generated in the emitter and core of MI cable due to emission of Compton and photo electrons by gamma environment needs correction. This is achieved by providing two cores in cable. The output current from both the conductors are subtracted by means of electronics. Differential current is actual output signal from the sensitive length of SPND. ECIL manufactures Self-Powered Neutron Detectors (SPND) with Vanadium, Inconel and Platinum emitters. Detectors along with MI Cable have been tested for hydrostatic pressure of 250 Kg/cm². The response time of the SPND depends upon the half-life of daughter nuclides responsible for electric current generation from SPND. The electrical current flow is due to either of the three interactions (n,b) ; (n,g, e) & (g, e)with incident Neutron. (n,γ,e) interaction produces a prompt electrical current signal while the(n.β) and (γ,e) interactions result in delayed electrical current signals. at 20°C: 1 x 10¹² Ω (min) between signal and compensating lead at 300°C: 5 x 10⁸ Ω (min) between signal and collector Gamma Ionization Chambers operate in ionization region of gas filled radiation detectors. The principle of operation is collection of charge generated during primary ionization created by incident gamma field in the gas volume between two electrodes having potential difference. ECIL make Gamma Ion chambers have robust mechanical design and are being used for area gamma monitoring and other industrial applications. The chambers are usually made of stainless steel SS304L or Aluminum material. The electrodes are made of Aluminum isolated using ceramic-metal seals. Guard ring technique is used between electrodes that results in low leakage current. The chamber will be made with pure Aluminum body, when the application is for use in a combined neutron-gamma field or when low-energy gamma is to be monitored. The chambers are normally filled with a mixture of high pure Nitrogen and Argon gases. Any other filling could be done as per the user requirement can be done. The chambers are terminated with coaxial HN series receptacles normally. Terminations other than HN can also be provided as per customer requirement. To meet radiation dose requirement, these chambers could be terminated with special connectors which could withstand 10 8 RAD dose. The gamma Ionization chambers are tested using standard Cs-137 gamma source to determine Voltage-Current saturation characteristics and the sensitivity. For most of the ionization chambers, the operating voltage region is usually 600 to 100V DC. The ionization chambers used for area gamma monitoring having low gamma fields are designed with hemispherical geometry to have better air kerma. Unless stated otherwise the geometry will be cylindrical. These chambers are fitted with HN series receptacles. Any other termination as required by the customer can also be supplied. Matching connectors that are suitable for 6 mm or 11 mm dia cables are supplied. The energy response of the detectors is usually tested in the range 60KeV to 1.3 MeV. This dual volume gamma ionization chamber could detect gamma field over 8 decades. The robust design of this chamber makes it operable in accident conditions inside the containment wall of Nuclear Reactor. The detector comprises two sensitive volumes. Sensitivity of one volume is 10 times more than other volume. The detector was qualified for IEC 60951-3(Equipment for continuous high range gamma monitoring during accident and post-accident conditions. The detector can withstand harsh emergency conditions and is designed to have a service life beyond 20 years. The chambers are usually made of stainless steel SS304L or Aluminum material. The electrodes are made of Aluminum isolated using ceramic-metal seals. Guard ring technique is used between electrodes that results in low leakage current. The fill gas is mixture of high pure Nitrogen and Argon gases. The chamber is integrated with Mineral(MgO) Insulated Cable terminated with LEMO twin contact connectors which could withstand radiationdose > 10⁸RAD. B12 is a gas-flow type ionization chamber for the detection of Tritium-in-Air. It is primarily designed for use in PHWRs. The two annular volumes between the three cylindrical electrodes mounted coaxially and insulated from one another by Teflon, constitute a Dual Ionization chamber consisting of two volumes (outer volume and inner volume). Both the volumes are kept nearly equal by design and are oppositely polarized during the use so that, the output of the chamber is less than 5% of the total in ambient gamma. During the usage, the detector is used as a sensor in the Tritium-In-Air monitoring system. The sample air is made to enter the outer volume which is sensitive and gets ionized by ‘Tritium + (other noble gas activities and background)’. A second flow of sample air is to flow through driers (i.e., Moisture Traps) and then through the inner volume. As the driers remove tritium, the inner volume will be sensitive to and give a current proportional to ‘other noble gas activities and background’. As the two volumes have electrically opposite polarization, the resultingdifferential output signal current from the chamber will be proportional to the ‘Tritium’ activity concentration, i.e. (Tritium + noble gas activity + background γ) - (noble gas activity + background γ). title: Reactor Instrumentation Control | ECIL | DAE | India
tags: Neutron Flux Monitoring for Intermediate & Power Range of Reactor Operations
Neutron Flux Monitoring for Reactor Startup Instrumentation
content: Nuclear Instrumentation is vital for the safe operation of nuclear reactors. Monitoring of neutron flux inside the core during the entire operation cycle of the reactor is essential for reactor start-up, control, protection, and failed fuel detection. Radiation monitoring at different locations inside the reactor and in the vicinity is mandatory for process control, worker safety, and public safety. The instrumentation required for processing the signals from sensors must have high reliability, low mean time to detect failures and meet stringent environmental conditions, including EMI/EMC and seismic/ vibration/ shock ECIL has been supplying the different types of Radiation Monitoring equipment required for all nuclear reactors in the country. The know-how for most of the systems has been obtained from BARC/NPCIL/IGCAR and other DAE organizations. ECIL has successfully engineered and qualified the equipment and manufactured them to meet the quality requirements. ECIL has also established state-of-the-art test facilities for qualifying and characterizing the instruments for reactor applications. The equipment includes: The source range (0.1nv to 106nv) monitoring of neutron flux is achieved by processing the detector (FC/10B/ 10BF3 counters) in pulse mode. These channels amplify the low-level signal by charge-sensitive pre-amplifiers (located near the detector). Alternately, fast current amplifiers are deployed for detectors with low collection time without a pre-amplifier. The pre-amplifier output is further processed to generate a 0 to 5-volt semi-gaussian shape. A low-level discriminator rejects the noise and gamma pile-up signals and is fed simultaneously to a Scaler Timer and a Log Count Rate Meter unit (LCRM), generating 0 to 10V DC output corresponding to an input frequency of 0.1 to 106 CPS. The Scaler Timer counts the number of pulses for a preset time. The output of LCRM is given to a Log Rate module to generate an inverse period signal. The channel creates alarm/trip signals (isolated logic outputs, relay contacts) for LCRM that are below an average value, higher than the set value, and a log rate higher than a set value. These channels also generate the detector bias voltage and regulated DC supplies for powering the modules. With a 4U height modular construction, extensive diagnostic features such as FIT, monitoring of a standard range of bias voltages, and built-in test signals for quick calibration checking are provided for fail-safe operation and low Mean Time to Detect and Repair any faults. These channels are qualified for EMC/EMI, seismic, vibration, and environmental conditions per IEC standards and operate reliably in harsh environments. The Neutronic Alarm Unit (NAU) is part of the Reactor Protection System (RPS). It trips the reactor whenever the Neutronic signals cross the predefined threshold limits. The system operates on DC power supplies of ±15V & 24V. It consists of the following modules- NAU receives Linear N, Log N, and Rate Log N signals from the Ion chamber amplifier. These signals are compared against the set thresholds to generate corrected Lin N high, Log N Low/High/Very High, and Rate Log N High/very high alarm contacts. Alarm indication LEDs are also provided at the front panel for local monitoring. The Unit also receives 14 ROP (Regional Over Power) signals from the ROP amplifiers. These ROP signals are averaged to produce a Bulk-N signal. This Bulk-N signal is compared with the set reference to generate alarm contacts. To avoid the contribution of faulty ROP signals in the averaging circuit, logic is built to include only those ROP signals in the averaging circuitry that are within the ‘HEALTHY’ window. The display module displays all the set points and signals on the analog or digital meters. The ROP amplifier is used to measure thermal neutron flux in the power range of a nuclear reactor. The ROP amplifier units are located in triplicated channel equipment rooms of the Main Control Center (MCC) and Back-up Control Centre (BCC) for the Reactor Protection System (RPS). The incident neutron flux on the detector gives low current signals. The amplifier receives these low-level current signals (emitter and compensating current input signals) from the ROP detector (Inconel SPND detectors), and it amplifies the signal to calibrate and read representative reactor thermal power. The amplifier output is 0.5-5V and 4-20mA for 0-150%FP. The amplifier also retransmits the amplified signals to generate Overpower Trip through the Regional Overpower Protection alarm system. It has a built-in test facility and a provision to assess the detector and cab. The ROP amplifier unit consists of 12 independent ROP amplifier modules mounted in a 4U NIM bin suitable for 19” rack mounting. It has undergone Environmental tests per IS 9000 part-III & V, a Seismic test, and EMI/EMC requirements per IEC-61000 standards. The Neutronic Alarm Unit (NAU) is part of the Reactor Protection System (RPS). It trips the reactor whenever the Neutronic signals cross the predefined threshold limits. The system operates on DC power supplies of ±15V & 24V. It consists of the following modules- NAU receives Linear N, Log N, and Rate Log N signals from the Ion chamber amplifier. These signals are compared against the set thresholds to generate corrected Lin N high, Log N Low/High/Very High, and Rate Log N High/very high alarm contacts. Alarm indication LEDs are also provided at the front panel for local monitoring. The Unit also receives 14 ROP (Regional Over Power) signals from the ROP amplifiers. These ROP signals are averaged to produce a Bulk-N signal. This Bulk-N signal is compared with the set reference to generate alarm contacts. To avoid the contribution of faulty ROP signals in the averaging circuit, logic is built to include only those ROP signals in the averaging circuitry that are within the ‘HEALTHY’ window. The display module displays all the set points and signals on the analog or digital meters. In-core neutron flux measurement system for 700MWe forms a part of reactor power regulating system and flux mapping system and helps in maintaining the desired flux shape. The local flux is measured by 122 no’s of SPNDs of Vanadium and Inconel as emitters. SPND amplifier units are used to monitor and process the signal representing neutron flux obtained from slow responding vanadium (Flux Mapping System (FMS)) and fast responding Inconel (Reactor Regulating System (RRS)). The main application of the SPND Amplifier is to continuously measure the neutron flux in the form of current coming from SPND detectors which is located inside Nuclear Reactor Core. The amplifier receives emitter lead and compensating lead current signals from SPND and operates in two selective ranges high power and low power range and subsequent GAIN stages to process the signals. Final output voltages and currents produced are proportional to the % of Reactor Power. These signals form controlling and regulating signals to subsequent stages of Reactor safety and criticality applications. The delayed Neutron Monitoring (DNM) System detects delayed Neutron presence in the primary coolant channels of PHWRs due to failed fuel elements with ruptured cladding. Samples are drawn selectively from individual coolant channels of all fuel channels. Samples from each channel flow in tubes adjacent to 10BF3 counter assemblies, which produce charge pulses in response to the delayed neutrons released from fission products. The charge pulses are amplified by Preamplifiers and are processed by Count Rate Meters (CRM) that give 0 to 10 VDC output signals, which are then fed to the control room computer for further processing. Also, the output data can be observed either in a Digital Panel Meter mounted on a Manual Data Collection Unit (MDCU) in “Remote” mode or at the output jacks of the CRM Bin in the “Local” mode setting. Control switches for Range, Time Constant, and Test Mode are provided on a separate unit called Function Control Unit (FCU) for use in “local” mode. High Voltage Power Supply (HVPS) provides operating voltage for seventeen nos. of 10BF3 counters. Except for the 10BF3 counters, all the other equipment can be mounted in a 19” wide instrument rack. Neutronic Instrumentation Channels are significantly required to measure the core thermal neutron flux during the following various stages of reactor operation during criticality and subsequent criticalities. It provides protection signals for shutting down reactor when the Neutronic parameters exceed set threshold values. NI Channels are subdivided based on the range of operation into pulse processing channels for Fission Counter(FC),Boron Coated counter BCC) and Helium-3 (He3) detectors and DC processing channels for Gamma Compensated Ion Chamber (GCIC) detectors The IRG monitor provides output signal on LCD and also generates visual / audio alarm locally for warning the working personnel, whenever preset limit is exceeded. It transmits information to upper level of ARMS for remote display The Intermediate/power range (104nv to 1010nv) monitoring of neutron flux is achieved by processing the detector (FC/10B/ ion chambers) in Mean Square Voltage (Campbell) or DC mode. These channels amplify the low-level signal by measuring the current and white noise content. The DC range is from 10-12 to 10-4 Amps and can be directly connected to the sensor for a maximum cable length of 100 meters. These units generate Log-Power, Linear-Power, and Log-Rate signals for reactor control and generate Trip/Alarm signals for reactor protection. These channels also generate the detector bias voltage and regulated DC supplies for powering the modules. With a 4U-high modular construction, extensive diagnostic features such as FIT, monitoring of a normal range of bias voltages, and built-in test signals for quick calibration checking are provided for fail-safe operation and low Mean Time to Detect and Repair any faults. These channels are qualified for EMC/EMI, seismic, vibration, and environmental conditions as per IEC standards and operate reliably in harsh environments. An in-core neutron flux measurement system for 500MWe and other Reactors forms a part of the reactor power regulating system and helps maintain the desired flux shape. The local flux is measured by 102 nos. of Self Powered Neutron Detectors (SPND) of Cobalt and Vanadium as emitters.12 nos. of SPND amplifiers housed in a 19-inch rack-mountable, 4U height bin, and an embedded PC with XP/QNX OS form a cluster. 9 nos. of such clusters are in the reactor building. Each cluster has dual Ethernet ports for redundancy, and in turn, these clusters communicate to the fault-tolerant redundant clients through hubs and switches located in the control room over FOC. The clients display the flux profile and send the requisite data for the reactor regulating system. The TIP (Travelling In-Core Probe) Detector - Amplifier system is required for calibration of SPNDs. It is also required for reactor low power physics experiments. TIP system is not in use during normal reactor operation. However, it is expected to be in operation at various occasions throughout the reactor life. This system is required for the reactor power from 10-6 FP to 10-3 FP (i.e. 0.1%FP) to provide useful information about flux shape in the reactor. The TIP amplifier will be used to amplify the current signal representing neutron flux received from TIP Detector (i.e Miniature Fission Chamber) in the reactor power range from 10-6 FP (i.e. 0.0001% FP) to 10-3 FP (i.e. 0.1% FP). Online Boron Concentration Meter (OLBM) measures the boron concentration present in the primary coolant of nuclear power plants. The Unit is mounted on the pipe carrying light water coolant. title: Nuclear Instrumentation Module | ECIL | DAE | India
content: The nuclear electronics industry has standardized the signal definitions, power supply voltages, and physical dimensions of basic nuclear instrumentation modules using the Nuclear Instrumentation Modules (NIM) standard initiated in the 1960s. NIM is the oldest and simplest nuclear electronics standard created in 1969 with AEC report TID20893 (Dec 1969); it defines a powered bin and plug-in modules. Two of the most essential advantages of the NIM concepts are flexibility and interchangeability. The user may configure the optimum system for a particular application and later quickly restructure the instruments as required for different experiments or measurements. In addition, an existing system can be updated with a few new modules, thereby augmenting the value of instrumentation. As experimental demands increase or as advancing technology makes new instruments available, new modules can be added to the system with assurance of compatibility. NIM instrumentation encompasses complete detector signal processing electronics from Preamplifier to Energy/Timing Spectroscopy. It is the perfect standard for small and flexible setups for high-resolution measurements with analog electronics, including amplifiers, high-resolution analog to digital converters, timing electronics, and low/high voltage supplies. NIM has been in use for small-laboratory nuclear science experiments to large-size particle accelerator-based nuclear physics experiments. ECIL has been the first in the country to develop this specialized class of modular instrumentation by effectively converting the R&D efforts at BARC into commercial viability. ECIL, at present, is a leading supplier of Nuclear Instrumentation Modules, which are presented in greater detail in this catalog. The range of NIM instrumentation supported by ECIL includes Mechanical Housing, Power Supply, and functional modules. Though this catalog describes only modules that are in regular production at ECIL, any specific NIM module not covered in this catalog can be supplied against the order. ECIL can meet any experimental requirement, from simple counting systems to high-resolution spectroscopy applications. With the personal computer, ECIL utilized the mechanical frame, power supply, computing power, and display capability of the PC to the fullest extent by building the pulse height analyzer initially as a PC Add-on Card and later as external hardware with a USB interface to the PC. The later version is in regular production. ECIL’s Modular Instrumentation Bin K2700N and Power Supply LV4753B have been designed as detachable parts to provide a NIM Powered Crate with mechanical and electrical facilities to accommodate various nuclear instrument modules. Up to 12 single-width modules or combinations can be accommodated. Carefully designed module guides facilitate the sliding-in and positioning of modules simultaneously, adding strength to the bin. The power supply (attachable) is conservatively rated to power any combination of modules that the bin will physically accommodate. The power on-off switch and the indicator lamp are conveniently located without sacrificing module space. Safety features include short circuit protection, over-voltage protection, and over-temperature protection. The ECIL’s Vehicle Monitoring System VMS 4030 is designed to detect nuclear materials and radioisotopes to stop an illicit shipment of Special Nuclear Material. It automatically screens vehicular traffic without the need for frequent calibration. The system has a camera to capture the vehicle image in alarm condition. This system is designed to meet ANSI N42.35 standards. The ECIL Model 4828 N 5-kV Detector Bias Supply furnishes bias voltage for germanium detectors, silicon detectors, or ionization chambers. It can be used with any detector that draws less than 100 μA of current and whose gain is insensitive to the applied voltage. ECIL’s High Voltage Unit HV 4831 B/N is a slow-rising, continuously variable high-voltage bias supply designed for operation with all types of detectors requiring up to +/ - 2500V bias and current up to 1mA. The ECIL Model PA 4850 Charge Sensitive Pre-Amplifier is designed for use with a wide range of detectors with capacitance from 1 pF to 100 pF. Its low noise and fast rise time it well-suited for energy spectroscopy applications. Shaping Amplifier is a single-width NIM module with pile-up rejecter, gated baseline restorer, auto threshold, diode-limited uni-polar and bi-polar output, visual aid for PZ cancellation, BUSY, and count rate output as some of the key features designed into it. The ECIL’s Spectroscopy Amplifier PA 4903N is a high-performance energy spectroscopy amplifier ideally suited for use with all types of detectors, such as germanium, Si(Li), and Si-charged particle detectors. It can also be used with scintillation detectors and proportional counters. This is a single-width module with a standard NIM connector. Frequency Timer Counter is used for counting the TTL pulses for a set time. This module receives TTL pulses and operates on 5V supply. Scalar timer module is a 7-digit counter that can count and Display counts upto 1MHz. Three thumb wheel switches mounted on the front panel of the module to set the counting time interval. The inbuilt optical to TTL conversion enables optical signal inputs from optical transmitters. The module consists of two LED indicators namely `OVERFLOW' and `TIMERON' mounted on the front panel. Starting of counting is through actuation of a spring-loaded START push button. Another spring loaded, resets the Scalar module and displays zero counts. Provision for RESET push button when pressed remote reset and start is available. title: NUCON Programmable Logic Controllers (PLC) | ECIL | DAE | India
content: NUCON PLC Platform has evolved by synergizing and harmonizing the design expertise at BARC, IGCAR and ECIL with several enhanced safety, security and diagnostics features incorporated in the design of the system. It is a modular and scalable PLC employing unified set of electronic hardware modules and running multiple software product lines meant for providing qualified solution for C&I systems of nuclear applications (NUCON-SA/NUCON-SB/NUCON-SC also called as NUCON-S series) and industrial solutions (NUCON-C). NUCON PLC hardware modules are qualified as per the IEC-61131-2 for EMI/EMC and environmental testing. It follows the specific recommendations for design of hardware as given in IEC-60987. The NUCON PLC software product line includes the in-house developed and qualified software modules for NUCON-S Series, and IEC 61131-3 standard qualified software modules for NUCON-C series. IEC 61131 Compliant GUI based programming software.; Supports all 5 Languages: LD, FBD, ST, IL & SFC; RT Linux based CodeSys programming engine.; In-house developed associated tasks. title: Remote Terminal Unit (RTU) | ECIL | DAE | India
content: ECRTU 100 is a Remote Terminal Unit (RTU) Indigenously designed and developed by ECIL.ECRTU provides the low cost solution to cater the needs of remote data collection / automated monitoring /controlling systems for low I/O counts. ECRTU offers a customized and cost-efficient solution for remote data collection applications. ECRTU is an ideal choice for the applications that require interfacing with intelligent devices and with a limited number of hardwired I/Os. The ECRTU is equipped with RS232/RS485 ports,10/100/1000 Mbps Ethernet communication ports. The availability of protocols like MODBUS TCP/IP, MODBUS Serial, DNP3, DNP3 SA, IEC 60870-5-101, IEC 60870-5-103, IEC 60870-5-104, IEC 61850, DLMS allows the integration with multi-vendor devices. The ECRTU has built-in analog and digital I/O for interfacing with local hardwired signals. All the I/O channels are isolated and surge-protected for use in electrically harsh environments. The digital inputs support Sequence of Events Recording, and the Digital Outputs Support Select-Before-Operate function. The analog input channels support DC voltage and current inputs. The Events/Alarms recorded by ECRTU are stored in a SD card memory along with the time stamps and can be communicated to central station. ECRTU supports all the five languages LD, FBD, ST, IL and SFC as per the IEC 61131-3 programming Standard. title: Instrumentation For Fuel Reprocessing Handling And Waste Management | ECIL | DAE | India
tags: Instrumentation For Fuel Reprocessing Handling And Waste Management
content: Fuel reprocessing facilities require specific instrumentation for Criticality monitoring, in-cell monitoring, Plutonium assaying, Nuclear Material Accounting systems etc in addition to the instrumentation required for nuclear reactors. This system is used for detecting criticality in fuel reprocessing plants by measuring sudden increase in gamma field using gamma ion chambers. The unit measures dose and dose rate and has independent alarm thresholds and criticality alarm is generated based on 2 out of 3 voting logic. The system comprises of three detectors (Ionization chambers), four power supply modules, three criticality monitors, one system alarm monitor consisting of Alarm module and Data acquisition module with 10.4” LCD display. These are arranged in 19” rack mountable BINs with three Ionization chambers kept in the monitoring zone of nearly 100 meters away from the system. Criticality monitors receive the signals from detectors and processing electronics generates local alarm when the dose or dose Rate exceeds the limit set by the threshold in case of criticality. When two out of three detectors give dose or dose rate high, the changeover contacts sends the alarm condition to system alarm unit. System Alarm generates audio and visual alarms. Criticality alarm contacts are also given to the remote console and to hooter. Data acquisition module receives and displays the parameters like criticality monitor’s individual status, healthiness of the batteries, test/operate condition, criticality, and alarm status data. The dose alarm is tested by creating a high intensity radiation field for a period of 500 milliseconds at ECIL. The system Complies with the IEC 860, ISO 7753, ANSI/ANS 8.3-1997 standards EMI/EMC and seismic qualified. The instrument consists of a detector unit and processing unit. The detector unit measures the radiation and converts into frequency. A CsI detector coupled with SiPM is used for radiation detection. A temperature compensated mechanism eliminates the fluctuations in pulse heights due to variation in temperatures. The processing unit converts the frequency signals into engineering data and display the same on the display. The unit is responsible for calibration curve fitting, Ethernet communication, history data storage etc. The instrument is in the advanced stage of testing. The Wide Range Gamma Monitor is an instrument used to measure and display the gamma radiation levels in the area where the detector of the instrument is installed. If the radiation level exceeds the alarm level set by the user, the instrument issues an audio-visual alarm to alert personnel in its vicinity. The instrument comprises of a wall-mountable Electronic Unit and a detachable Detector Probe. The detailed technical specifications are given in the following table. The dual channel Alpha/Beta Continuous Air Monitor (CAM) is intended to use in Nuclear Power Plants, Reprocessing Plants, Fuel Storage and other Nuclear Facilities for measuring releases of air particulate radioactivity from the facility. The real time inputs provided by the monitor help to verify the integrity of the reactor containment system and ensure early warning of workers, if the containment is breached. It announces audio/visual alarms on exceeding set values of annual limit intake of worker with calculated, Derived Air Concentration (DAC) and Exposure (DAC-h). With the help of sampling probes, the CAM can also be used for monitoring particulate activity in applications like stack monitoring, where higher sampling flow rate from 30 LPM to greater than 100 LPM is required. Plutonium Continuous Air Monitor (Pu-CAM) is a critical component of the air monitoring program in all laboratories dealing with plutonium (Pu)in powder form such as reprocessing facilities, fast reactor fuel fabrication facilities etc. Intelligent Accessible Area Radiation Monitor (IAARM) is provided to monitor radiation field in the accessible areas of Reactor Building. The system is used to monitor the Dose Rate and provide audio-visual alarm for warning the working personnel locally/remote whenever preset limit is exceeded. Analog and potential free contact outputs are also provided for local/remote annunciation. A local Keypad cum Display unit is provided on the Monitor for local user interface. Facility for the monitoring /control /programming/setting of parameters shall be provided by the Monitor through Digital Interface (Ethernet communication) from local Keypad as well as for remote operation from RADAS. ECIL Radiation Counting System, RCS 4037 is a microcontroller-based system. This unit can be used either with GM Counter or Photo multiplier tubes to detect and display radioactivity through the use of the detector probe SP 647A and the GM tube LND72314. It is an all-solid state compact instrument making extensive use of integrated circuit chips. The Count recorded or elapsed time is indicated on 16X2 LCD Display. The instrument designed as a self- contained unit and incorporates an electronically regulated high voltage supply to polarize the Alpha and GM probe. The supply ranges between 50 to 1500V DC in steps of 1V. . The Preset Timer provided in the unit has a range of 1 to 9999 Sec Selectable in step. 1 Sec. Drum Monitor assists in monitoring & Control disposal of the wastes in plants handling plutonium and uranium. The Passive Neutron Assay based waste Drum Monitor offers reliable & efficient assay of waste arising from nuclear reactors allowing classifications of wastes according to disposal category based on activity. The system is designed for ease of use and can be operated safely with minimum training requirement. The principle of operation of the System consists of thermalizing the fast neutrons emitted from the active waste (spontaneous fission Pu) by a polyethylene moderator containing thermal neutron detectors. The counts (or the neutron flux) are measure of the curie strength of the Pu in the drum. Pre-calculated correction factors are applied for the type of material filled in the drum. The assay system framework consists of a semicircular base on which the HDPE sheets can be stacked after machining to the appropriate shape. The system was designed using 8 Nos. of 3He or BF3 detectors of length 1 meter & 3.75cm Diameter. All the detectors are placed equidistant from each other in a semicircular geometry. A pulse amplifier module is used for amplification of current pulses from the detector & discriminates the noise & other unwanted pulses such as gamma and generates the TTL Pulses of frequency proportional to the neutron content present in the waste. The pulses are fed to the counter present in the microcontroller module for Counting and analysis purpose. The system is interfaced with the PC through RS232 or RS 485 communication. The system responds to the commands given by the PC to START & STOP the waste analysis. In-cell monitors are required for monitoring and assessing the radiation dose inside the cells of Radio Chemical plants. It consists of a wall mounted electronics unit with displays and controls and an extended detector probe with a cable of at least 30 meters. The alarm level setting is carried out through RS-485 serial port/ Ethernet with a hand-held configurator or PC with password Protection. The monitor has a RS-485(MODBUS/RTU) serial communication port and Ethernet (TCP/IP) port for interfacing with a PC and other units in multi drop network. The PC and the monitor will operate in a hot-slave configuration in a multi-drop network through this interface. The configuration settings will be password protected and the password will be user defined. The monitor is having built-in self-diagnostics. On being powered it will perform tests to ensure that all components and sub systems are functioning properly. title: Security & Safeguard Instrumentation Systems | ECIL | DAE | India
content: Monitoring nuclear and other radioactive material carried by pedestrians, vehicles, trains, and other transportation methods is essential to deter, detect, and prevent illegal trafficking. ECIL has developed various stationary systems for detecting fissile and radioactive materials at border checkpoints, airports, and ship ports. These are also used at different nuclear installations, metallurgical, and waste processing plants to detect the accidental disposition of isotopes in scrap metal facilities or solid waste landfills. The building block of the system is the Radiation Detection Panel (RDP), comprising of a single, large-area plastic scintillator. Two numbers of such RDPs form one doorway monitoring system, whereas 4 numbers, along with neuron detectors, are used for the Vehicle Monitoring system for container scanning. This Modular architecture allows easy expansion and integration for a range of subjects (pedestrian, cargo, train, etc.). One no’ of LINUX-based electronic processing unit (EPU), common for all RDPs, is located inside one RDP. The EPU receives the signals from all RDPs to measure and process, stores the signals from each RDP, and generates an alarm when the radioactivity measured exceeds the background by a certain limit. While the EPU is a stand-alone unit, it also sends the data to a remote PC for recording, storing data, and generating the reports in the prescribed format. The EPU performs tasks such as analyzing the detectors' pulses, managing data received from the detector assemblies, and configuring the system's operational parameters in real-time. With high-speed Signal processing and alarm analysis, these systems provide a high detection capability. The doorway monitoring and vehicle Monitoring System also has IR occupancy sensors. During an unoccupied state, the system measures the background radiation field and uses this information to detect any presence of radioactive material when occupied. The pedestrian and vehicle monitors are equipped with cameras to grab pictures of pedestrians and vehicles when found to carry radioactive material above the Minimum Detectable Quantity (MDQ). Qualified to meet the EMC/EMI, weather, corrosion, and other tests as per ANSI N42.35 standards, these systems manufactured by ECIL have been tested and evaluated at various locations to meet the MDQ limits and have been found to have very low false alarm rate. Once detected, the quantification and identification are carried out by hand-held isotope identifiers using NaI scintillators. The ECIL’s Vehicle Monitoring System VMS 4030 is designed to detect nuclear materials and radioisotopes to stop an illicit shipment of Special Nuclear Material. It automatically screens vehicular traffic without the need for frequent calibration. The system has a camera to capture the vehicle image in alarm condition. This system is designed to meet ANSI N42.35 standards. The LINUX-based electronic processing unit (EPU), common for all RDPs, is inside one RDP. The EPU receives the signals from all RDPs, measures, processes, and stores the signals from each RDP, and generates an alarm when the radioactivity measured exceeds the background by a certain limit. While the EPU is a stand-alone unit, it also sends the data to a remote PC to record, store, and generate the reports in the prescribed format. The EPU performs tasks such as analyzing the detectors' pulses, managing data received from the detector assemblies, and configuring the system's operational parameters, all in real-time. With high-speed Signal processing and alarm analysis, these systems provide a high detection capability. An alarm log is recorded in an internal memory. Alarm events include: Monitor IDTime and date Gamma count rate from all detectors individually and background levels for each Maximum gamma count rate associated with the occupancy that triggered the alarm Image of the vehicle carrying the radioactive material Doorway Monitor PMS 4021 was developed to safeguard and account for Special Nuclear Material (SNM), even in very small quantities, to prevent its unauthorized movement and illegal trafficking by pedestrians. This system is required at entry/exit points of nuclear facilities and ports of the country, such as Airports and seaports, Border Control, and Customs checkpoints. This monitor helps detect any radioactive material carried by persons or cheeking hand luggage The software in the external PC is configured to log alarm events consisting of Monitor ID, Time and date, Gamma count rate from all detectors individually and background levels for each, Maximum gamma count rate associated with the occupancy that triggered the alarm, and the - image of the person carrying the radioactive material. ECIL’s Radiation Monitor RM4564A is a rugged, lightweight, and portable radiation survey meter cum contamination monitor designed to monitor nuclear radiation (Beta & Gamma), where radioactive elements are being handled. Once the limb monitor/doorway monitor/vehicle monitor detects any radioactive material, this unit can be used to precisely locate and measure the radiation level. This can also be used for Beta surface contamination and Beta radioactive concentration. It can store 500 readings & can be retrieved with serial number and time stamping. These instruments consist of: ECIL is regularly supplying the above types of low-cost Radiation Monitoring equipment, and these are qualified for applicable environmental conditions. While keeping stress on reduction in the cost, efforts are made to incorporate the technological advances resulting in new types of microcontroller-based instruments have been developed with RS 485 and ETHERNET connectivity. Area Radiation Monitoring is most important in Electron Accelerator, where the radiation is the outcome of Accelerator beam spill. Since the radiation is of pulsed in nature, ionization chamber as detector is more suitable as It responds linearly to short duration pulses and useful to monitor environment in the control room in area of an accelerator. The purpose of the area monitor AM4561A is to continuously monitor radiation levels of specified occupancy locations and to provide alarm if a preset level exceeds. These monitors located at different places, ensure personal radiological safety in accelerator environment. BM 4560, which has lower sensitivity, is used as beam loss monitor for Storage Ring tunnel The AGRM (Area Gamma Radiation Monitor) provides an output proportional to the dose rate of gamma-emitting radio-nuclide present in Nuclear Power plant premises and process pipelines for local display on measured values in Sv/hr or Gy/hr and transmits the same to upper-level of ARMS for remote display. It also provides audio & visual alarms with an external alarm unit for warning personnel whenever the preset limit is exceeded. The Accident Monitor is used for measurement of gamma radiation in the reactor building during normal, accident and post-accident condition. The equipment continuously monitors the absorbed dose rate of gamma radiation and display on the unit value proportional to radiation level for local indication and remote display. It also provides audio/visual alarms locally for warning the working personnel whenever preset limits are exceeded. title: Liquid Effluent Monitors | ECIL | DAE | India
content: Liquid activity monitors detect and measure radioactive contamination within liquid samples, providing critical information for radiation safety and environmental protection. In nuclear power plants, laboratories, medical facilities, and environmental monitoring agencies, these monitors help to ensure that any radioactive substances in liquids are identified, quantified, and controlled to prevent potential health and environmental risks. These monitors function by using various detection methods suited to specific types of radiation, such as alpha, beta, or gamma emissions. Each method is chosen based on the type of radiation and sensitivity required for the application, whether monitoring waste streams, effluents, cooling water, or environmental water samples. The Liquid Effluent Monitor is used for continuous measurement of volumetric activity of gamma emitting radio-nuclides present in liquid of different process systems like liquid radioactive waste processing system, contaminated section of active laundry, automated chemical monitoring system & discharge channel etc. A scintillation detector is used to measure the sample of effluent liquid from a tank or a pool. The unit is designed to use as one of the field instruments at lower level of Modbus network-based Automated Radiation Monitoring System (ARMS) in Kudankulam Nuclear Power Plant Units 3 & 4. The monitor is available in two types - one type is developed to use in waste water flow tanks and the other type is to install in a permutated tube located at effluent releases to the sea. The LEM (Liquid Effluent Radiation Monitor) is designed for continuous measurement of volumetric activity of gamma emitting radio-nuclides present in liquid of different process systems like liquid radioactive waste processing system, contaminated section of active laundry, automated chemical monitoring system for steam generator blow down system, siphon wells & discharge channel etc. It provides output proportional to volumetric activity of gamma emitting radio-nuclides present in liquid media for local indication and transmits the same to upper level of ARMS for remote display. It also provides audio/visual alarms locally for warning the working personnel whenever preset limits are exceeded. The measurement range of detection is from 103 Bq/m3 to 106 Bq/m3. The Liquid Effluent Monitors are connected to the gateways through daisy chaining and then to the centralized ARMS server. Process Water Discharge Activity Monitor measures the gamma activity of Liquids flowing through Tubes/Pipes. Using a Na(I) scintillator as the detector, these units measure the gross Gamma Activity of Energy Range from 50kev to 10Mev. The system hardware consists of: Sampling liquid from a pipe, a tank or a pool; Liquid gamma Isotopes: Cs-137, Co-60 and Co-57; Selectable Isotopes of measurement; Embedded Am-241 source for energy spectrum stabilization against temperature changes & aging; Seismic qualified: IEC 60980; EMI/EMC: IEC61000-4 series Scintillator and photomultiplier (integral assembly) with pre-amplifier and test signal generator housed in an aluminium tube; Detector bias supply module, pulse shaping amplifier module, linear count rate meter module with alarm generation circuitry and L.V.Supply module housed in a 4U height bin 0-10CPS corresponding to 0 to 6.25 pCi/cc; 0-100CPS corresponding to 0 to 62.5 pCi/cc; 0-1KCPS corresponding to 0 to 625 pCi/cc; 0-10KCPS corresponding to 0 to 6.25 nCi/cc; 0-100KCPS corresponding to 0 to 62.5 nCi/cc Description | Specification Detector | Scintillator- NaI(Tl) Type of radiation to be monitored | Gamma Radiation Energy Range | 0.66 to 1.5 MeV Range of measurement of volumetric activity | 4.0 x 10 3 to 4.0 x 10 6 Bq/m³ for FLOW THROUGH type 2.5 x 10 3 to 2.5 x 10 6 Bq/m³ for SUBMERSIBLE type Accuracy | ± 30% Front panel | OLED display Degree of Ingress Protection | DU-IP 68 DPU-IP 65 Power Consumption | 25VA Power Supply | 220VAC (-15% to 10%), 50Hz±3%.
