content: Air activity monitors detect and measure radioactive contamination in the air, particularly in environments where radiation exposure is a potential risk. These monitors help protect workers, the public, and the environment by continuously or periodically sampling the air for radioactive particles and gases. The air activity monitoring is suitable for applications in industries such as nuclear power, nuclear fuel handling facilities, medical facilities, research labs, mining. Air activity monitors come in various forms, each specialized for different applications and types of radiation. Continuous air monitors, particulate monitors, noble gas monitors, iodine monitors, radon detectors, and portable air samplers are some examples. These devices use various detection methods such as ionization chambers, scintillation detectors, and semiconductor-based spectroscopy to provide accurate, real-time data on airborne radioactivity levels. Tritium in Air Monitor monitors Tritium activity in the form of Tritium Oxide present in the sample air stream drawn from various areas of the nuclear plants and stack of a PHWR based Nuclear Power Plant. The unit provides local display of tritium activity concentration in DAC (Derived Activity Concentration) and analog signal outputs for remote display. The sample air, in addition to tritium may contain noble gas activities like Argon-41, Xenon 133/135 and Krypton 85. Hence the tritium activity monitor shall be capable of detecting tritium activity alone in presence of these Noble gas activities which are sometimes predominant. The approximate activity of these gasses is of the order of 300pCi/cc-400pCi/cc. Stack Activity Monitoring System monitors concentration of Particulate, Iodine-131, Argon-41 and Fission Product Noble Gas (FPNG) activities released through stack. All the equipment associated with stack activity monitoring system are located in Stack Activity Monitoring Room near stack. Stack activity monitoring system consists of following equipments: Sample air for monitoring is drawn from the stack (at 124.5M EL.) and passed through moisture trap. The sample air contains fine droplets of water (moisture). Moisture Trap will be connected in series with the sample line before the monitor so that if any droplet of water is present (in the sample air), it will be collected in the Moisture Trap. By this, droplets will not enter in the detector assembly. Then this sample enters a Particulate Filter Detector Assembly, Iodine Filter Detector Assembly, Gamma Detector Assembly, Flow Gauge (rotameter) and then it is returned back to the stack by vacuum pump. Alternate path for sample flow is provided by employing standby equipment. This equipment is provided to continuously monitor the Particulate activity released through Stack. This equipment is provided to continuously monitor Iodine 131 activity released through Stack. This equipment is provided to monitor gamma activities released through stack. Provision exists in the equipment to monitor concentrations of Fission Product Noble Gas(FPNG) activities and Argon activity present in the air stream. The system provides indications of both FPNG and Argon activity concentrations, release rate and cumulative release. Iodine monitor (Stationary & Mobile version) used for measuring Iodine volumetric activity in NPP. The measurement Range of the instrument is 1 to 104 Bq/m3 by the method of accumulation over 6 hrs and 0.1 to 105 Bq/m3 by the method of Observation. The equipment provides output signal on current value of volumetric activity of the iodine radio nuclides for display and also generates audio/visual alarms locally for warning the working personnel whenever preset limit is exceeded. It transmits information for remote display. The Alpha Beta Air Particulate (Aerosol) Monitor is designed for continuous measurement of volumetric activity of radioactive aerosols containing artificial Alpha and Beta emitting nuclides. It also indicates the effective equivalent concentration of Rn-222 in air for indoor application. It displays and transmits the concentration levels and generates audio visual alarms when radiation level exceeds a limit set by the user. It also transmits the data to upper-level systems through serial communication network. The monitor will have two types viz. Stationary unit and Mobile unit. The Inert Radio Active Gas (IRG) monitor is provided for continuous measurement of the volumetric activity of beta emitting inert radio-active gases (argon, krypton, xenon) in the air of controlled areas as well as in ventilation system, pipelines, stacks etc. The IRG monitor provides output signal on LCD and also generates visual / audio alarm locally for warning the working personnel, whenever preset limit is exceeded. It transmits information to upper level of ARMS for remote display. Plutonium Continuous Air Monitor (Pu-CAM) is a critical component of the air monitoring program in all laboratories dealing with plutonium (Pu) in powder form such as reprocessing facilities, fast reactor fuel fabrication facilities etc. Portable version of the monitor with plastic scintillator, light guide and SiPM is developed. content: An Environmental Radiation Monitor (ERM) consists of a Scintillation Detector Assembly with a Photomultiplier Tube, Pre-amplifier, and Electronic Processing and Display Unit. The monitors are in open areas and are designed with suitable enclosures to withstand harsh environmental conditions (direct sunlight, rain, dust, etc.). They provide a local display of a radiation field and signal output for remote display. The measurement range of detection is from 103 Bq/m3 to 106 Bq/m3. The Liquid Effluent Monitors are connected to the gateways through daisy chaining and then to the centralized ARMS server. The automated Environmental Radiation Monitoring System (AERMS) is intended for measuring radiation levels around the plant area and transmitting data to the Automated Radiation Monitoring System (ARMS) Upper-Level system and Onsite Emergency Support Centre (OESC). AERMS mainly includes Environmental Radiation Monitors (ERM), Battery Backup Control Units (BBCU), and Data Controller Units (DCU). The Data Controller Unit consists of a Controller, FX converters & PSDU Unit, which Receives integrated dose rates from Various ERMs located around the Plant area. title: Contamination Monitors | ECIL | DAE | India
content: Personnel contamination monitors are developed to use in radiation-controlled environments to detect and measure radioactive contamination on individuals’ skin, clothing, or equipment. These are critical for nuclear power plants, fuel handling & recycling facilities, research laboratories etc. for maintaining safety protocols by ensuring the radioactive particles are not inadvertently spread outside controlled areas. This type of monitoring safeguards workers, minimizes environmental contamination, and helps facilities meet regulatory safety standards. Personnel contamination monitors come in various designs and functionalities, catering to different levels of contamination detection and types of radiation. Each type of the monitor encapsulates with sensitive radiation detectors, such as scintillation or Geiger-Muller detectors, that can identify trace contamination by measuring ionizing radiation. Many models are equipped with audible or visual alarms to alert users if contamination is detected, prompting decontamination measures before exiting a controlled area. This catalogue provides a range of personnel contamination monitors to meet various application needs, from individual hand and foot checks to full-body screening solutions, supporting the nuclear facility’s safety protocols with reliable, industry-compliant monitoring equipment. The Hand and Foot contamination monitor is controller based radiation detection system that quickly measures Beta and Gamma contamination on the hands and foot/shoes of personnel working in radioactive environments. It measures activity and warns in case of excessive contamination so that quick emergency decontamination measures can be initiated. The system consists of four detector assemblies for monitoring hands & feet. The output pulses from the pan-cake type GM detectors are fed to the microcontroller system. The microcontroller continuously measures the background radioactivity and updates the counts. When a person stands on the platform and inserts his hands in the detector assemblies, background counting is interrupted; activity monitoring is performed for a time pre-settable from one second upwards. Measured counts are corrected for background activity, the information is processed for display, and an alarm is enunciated on the panel. The various parameters, such as the counting time and alarm limits can be set from setting menu on display. Additional facilities have been provided to check the performance of individual G.M. detectors to aid in the maintenance of the equipment. This system is installed at the final exit points of nuclear power plants and monitors personnel leaving these areas hand, foot, head, and body contamination. The system detector assemblies are mounted on a suitable frame, and dedicated microcontrollers process the data. The master microcontroller interacts with the PC’s leading software and gives instructions to start and stop the counters and reading signals through microcontrollers interconnected through the I 2 C bus. title: Portable Instruments | ECIL | DAE | India
content: Varieties of nuclear radiation monitoring instrumentation are required for DAE facilities, educational institutions, hospitals, defence and other industries using radioactive materials. These instruments consist of: ECIL is regularly supplying the above types of low-cost Radiation Monitoring equipment, and these are qualified for applicable environmental conditions. While keeping stress on reduction in the cost, efforts are made to incorporate the technological advances resulting in new types of microcontroller-based instruments have been developed with RS 485 and ETHERNET connectivity. Gamma Radiography Survey Meter MR 4500A is an instrument specially designed to measure gamma ray exposure rates. The instrument consists of a miniature energy compensated halogen quenched G.M. Tube as gamma ray detector and a count rate meter. The output of the count rate meter is displayed on a panel meter and is calibrated directly in terms of exposure rates. The instrument’s response is energy independent in the energy range of 80 KeV to 1330 KeV. This portable instrument is modified and works on three 1.5-volt cells (Eveready type 1035 or equivalent). This survey meter is useful for measuring exposure rates in occupied places around radiographic installations, measuring leakage radiation levels around the cameras, tracing lost sources and as a general-purpose survey meter. The Radiation Survey Meter MR4515 has been designed for measurement of low beta-gamma radiation levels. The instrument is portable, dry battery operated and self-contained. The exposure rate can be directly read on a micro ammeter. The GM detector used in this unit is of the thin-walled type and a rotating shutter provides the facility for beta-gamma discrimination. ECIL’s Radiation Monitor RM4564A is a rugged, lightweight, and portable radiation survey meter cum contamination monitor designed to monitor nuclear radiation (Beta & Gamma), where radioactive elements are being handled. This unit can be used to precisely locate and measure the radiation level. This can also be used for Beta surface contamination and Beta radioactive concentration. It can store 500 readings & can be retrieved with serial number and time stamping. ECIL’s alpha monitor CM4553A is designed for routine checking of radioactive contamination on workbenches, walls, beams etc. in active laboratories. The scintillation head for detection of alpha contamination is a large probe with a viewing area of about 100sq.Cms. It will be used in all laboratories. SP647A is a compact and rugged unit combining a scintillator and a low noise photomultiplier for alpha activity of samples. The scintillator use is a silver activated zinc sulphide coated on Perspex disc. The photomultiplier tube (VI-EMI-9656KB) is so arranged that all the detected scintillations on the scintillator will be focused through a specially designed reflector assembly to the cathode of the photomultiplier tube thus ensuring high efficiency. A detachable drawer type assembly has been arranged at the base to hold the samples and the scintillator in a light assembly. The source holder has been provided in the drawer to accommodate the samples i.e. Filter paper having thickness upto 2.5 mm and diameter 38 mm. However, samples of 0.5 mm thickness should be placed directly on the aluminium disc. For samples whose thickness is more than 2.5 mm are to be analyzed, the aluminum disc in the drawer will have to be substituted by one of suitable thickness, however the optimum gap between sample and sensitive screen is 2 mm. Scintillometer SM 141E is a rugged, lightweight and portable scintillometer designed for radiometric, geophysical and environmental reconnaissance surveys. The Micro-controller-based design employs accurate measurement of radiation levels and the large crystal volume employs reliable statistics. Based on a patented design from BARC, the digital pocket dosimeter employs a novel design using silicon rectifier diode as a radiation detector. The incident ionizing radiation is converted electrical impulses, a low power pulse amplifier, that amplifies the electrical pulses from the detector to detectable amplitudes, a discriminator circuit, that is used to reject pulses of origin other than those caused by the ionising radiation, a programmable divider circuit for calibrating the dosemeter, an electronic counting circuit and a six-digit LCD display. The sensitivity of the dosemeter is 1 count per μSv (micro-Sievert) and the accuracy is within ±15% from 60 keV to 1.25 Mev of X or Gamma radiation. A metallic energy compensation filter and a discriminator threshold modulation circuit are used to provide uniform response within ±15% from 60 KeV to 1.25 MeV. The Digital display indicates at any instant the total X or Gamma radiation dose, in μSv, received by the dosemeter since the time at which the dosemeter was switched on. The dosemeter is designed for very low power consumption and is powered by two-coin type Li batteries (Type CR2320). It is capable of over 500 hours of continuous operation before having to replace the batteries. A blinking LED indicates low battery condition when 8 hours of battery life is still left. The entire circuitry and the battery holder are mounted on a single printed circuit board. Surface mount components are used to make the unit compact. The dosemeter is compact (110 mm L×30 mm W×14 mm H excluding Clip) and light in weight (60 gm) The real time personal dosimeter system is intended to use for monitoring the real time dose/dose rate from the personnel working in remote locations. The system consists of three sub systems viz: Wireless pocket dosimeter, LORA (Long-Range, Low-Power) receiver and PC software to manage more no of wireless pocket dosimeters. The low power wireless dosimeter is developed with tiny power micro-controller, SiPM, CsI scintillator and LORA module. The micro controller measures the radiation, converts into engineering units and transmits the information using LORA modem. It also displays the dose and dose rate along with date and time stamp on TFT display. It generates audio alarm when the dose and dose rate values exceed the limits set through PC. The micro controller also issues the commands to LORA Radio modem to transmit the data in encrypted form. The LORA receiver receives the data from multiple numbers of pocket dosimeters and few receivers are to be placed at vantage pints and are connected to a common gateway, which in turn communicates to a central server for monitoring the dose received by person and also/dose rate to control the movement of the person. The instrument is in the advanced stage of testing. Neutron Rem Monitor (NRM100) is a Battery powered, Portable Instrument developed for monitoring radiation in the areas surrounding reactors, accelerators and other neutron producing equipment and neutron sources. NRM100 is based on classic Andersson Braun technique and measures Ambient Dose equivalent rate H*(10) as per guidelines mentioned in IEC 61005. The Instrument consists of BF3 / He3 Neutron Detector, mounted within the moderator and associated electronics. Electronics mainly consists of Charge sensitive Pre-Amplifier & Amplifier circuit, Processing unit, High Voltage supply & Battery Charger. The instrument is featured to display Dose Equivalent Rate & Accumulated Dose, RS232 Communication and TREND recording. NRM100 is RISC Microcontroller based Instrument. Micro-controller-based Battery charger unit provides an accurate 3-stage charge to battery and reduces risk of overcharging them. The temperature sensor attached on battery further refines the charge profile for correct charging under a variety of conditions. A bicolor LED indicates charging status. Processing unit monitors battery status periodically and indicates low battery on LCD display. title: Spectroscopic Instruments | ECIL | DAE | India
content: Liquid activity monitors detect and measure radioactive contamination within liquid samples, providing critical information for radiation safety and environmental protection. In nuclear power plants, laboratories, medical facilities, and environmental monitoring agencies, these monitors help to ensure that any radioactive substances in liquids are identified, quantified, and controlled to prevent potential health and environmental risks. These monitors function by using various detection methods suited to specific types of radiation, such as alpha, beta, or gamma emissions. Each method is chosen based on the type of radiation and sensitivity required for the application, whether monitoring waste streams, effluents, cooling water, or environmental water samples. The Liquid Effluent Monitor is used for continuous measurement of volumetric activity of gamma emitting radio-nuclides present in liquid of different process systems like liquid radioactive waste processing system, contaminated section of active laundry, automated chemical monitoring system & discharge channel etc. A scintillation detector is used to measure the sample of effluent liquid from a tank or a pool. The unit is designed to use as one of the field instruments at lower level of Modbus network-based Automated Radiation Monitoring System (ARMS) in Kudankulam Nuclear Power Plant Units 3 & 4. The monitor is available in two types - one type is developed to use in waste water flow tanks and the other type is to install in a permutated tube located at effluent releases to the sea. The Alpha Beta Air Particulate Monitor is designed for continuous measurement of volumetric activity of radioactive aerosols containing artificial Alpha and Beta emitting nuclides. It also measures effective equivalent in air for Rn-222 concentration for indoor application. It displays and transmits this concentration level, and generates audio visual alarms, when radiation level exceeds a limit set by the user. The monitor will have two versions namely, Stationary unit and Mobile unit. The Inert Radio Active Gas (IRG) monitor is provided for continuous measurement of the volumetric activity of beta emitting inert radioactive gases (argon, krypton, xenon) in the air of controlled areas as well as in ventilation system, pipelines, stacks etc. The IRG monitor provides output signal on LCD and also generatesvisual / audio alarm locally for warning the working personnel,whenever preset limit is exceeded. It transmits information to upper level of ARMS for remote display. The portable radio Isotope Identifier device is specialized for use in the health physics, law enforcement and homeland security. The System provides simple operation for the first responder who needs to react quickly and also provides detailed analyses for the sophisticated technical user. The PRID helps operators feel comfortable using the instrument even in the most hazardous and stressful environments. Several modes of operation give all users the information they need right at their fingertips. The basic functionality of the PRID is to detect, quickly locate, measure, and identify the source of radioactive material. title: Ship & Submarine Applications | ECIL | DAE | India
content: The Radiation Detection System for SSK Class of Submarines is designed with state-of-the-art technology to monitor Gamma radiation in and around the submarine to provide an early warning and a full appreciation to radiological hazards to the submarine. It enables the command to take appropriate counter measures. The System is capable of measuring radiation level up to 9.99 Gy/hr. There are total of 2 Detector assemblies of which one detector is placed inside the submarine and the other Detector Unit is placed on the Mast of the Submarine which can with stand up to 50 bar pressure. Provision has given to alter the Factory Set Alarm Level which is password protected. Alarm Condition Data will be printed on the Thermal Printer with Date & Time Stamping. title: High Voltage DC Power Supplies | ECIL | DAE | India
content: ECIL is India's preferred supplier of Power Electronics Equipments to various Nuclear Power Plants and International Scientific Programs like FAIR, ITER etc., ECIL has built various High Power Electronic Equipment ranging from High Voltage DC Power Supplies, Ultra stable High Voltage Power Converters, Four-Channel Flash X-Ray, 50 kW Induction Heating Inverter, 110 KVA Variable Frequency Drive, Electromagnetic Manufacturing System etc., HVPS is based on Pulse Step Modulation (PSM) technology with 12 pulse rectification. HVPS use multi-secondary transformers and Switched Power Modules (SPS). The modules will be forced water cooled and stacked on HV Rack(s). The HVPS uses the modular construction with all solid state (IGBT) switches for regulation as well as protection. HVPS is used to supply DC Power of various voltage and current ratings based on specifications. ECIL supplied the following HVPS systems: The dual output HVPS will convert the electrical power coming from the 22 kV AC electrical networks into DC power. The HVPS will be able to supply DC power to the driver and end stage of each RF source with voltages respectively up to 18 kV and 27 kV. HVPS consists of Multi-Secondary transformers (2 Nos, 2.8 MVA with 32 secondaries and 1.2 MVA with 16 secondaries), Switched Power Supply (SPS) Modules (48 Nos, 695 V, 190 A, 132 kW each) and FPGA/Real Time based controller. Acceleration Grid Power Supplies (AGPS) provide (-) 96kV to the Neutral beam sources of ITER and SPIDER for acceleration of negative ions with specific modulation. PSM based (-) 96kV/75A AGPSs supplied by ECIL to ITER-India and NBTF Facility, Italy. AGPS consists of Multi-Secondary Transformers (3 Nos, 2.8MVA each), Switched Power Supply (SPS) Modules (150Nos, 60kW each), FPGA/Real Time based controller. AGPS is controlled by 9 powerful synchronous FPGAs managed by real time controller to support low ripple, high resolution, programmable rise time, fast dynamics, full depth modulation, fast switching off and fast (~few milliseconds) re-application in case of breakdowns. The Acceleration Grid Power supply (AGPS) for Diagnostic Neutral Beam provides a negative voltage up to (-)96KV w.r.t ground to the beam source for acceleration of negative ions with specific modulation. This Power supply is based on PSM (Pulse Step Modulation) technique with 12 pulse rectification and uses the modular construction with IGBT switches for regulation & protection. The AGPS will convert the electrical power coming from the 22kV AC electrical networks into DC power. The AGPS will be able to supply DC power (7.2MW) to the Accelerator grids up to (-) 96kV. The output voltage will achieve the performances in term of accuracy, ripple and modulation. The AGPS will be able to regulate the voltage independently and also limits the energy to fault in case of breakdown. The AGPS consists of Multi-Secondary transformers (3 nos, 2.8MVA each), AC-DC converters (150 nos, 60 kW each) and FPGA/Real Time based controller. The other components of the AGPS includes AC Disconnector / Earthing Switch, HV Cables (AC), LV Cables (AC), High Voltage Rack, Passive protection component (Current limiting Inductor), DC Co-axial Cable, DC Disconnector / Earthing Switch, Equipment Control Cubicles, Dummy Load. Regulated High Voltage Power Supply (RHVPS) (-) 100kV, 25A used as cathode supply for Klystron. This Power Supply is based on Pulse Step Modulation (PSM) Topology with Multi secondary transformers and multiple Switched Power supply modules. EMM System is the state of art technology for shaping and joining of metals based on the Electromagnetic Forming (EMF) and Electromagnetic Welding (EMW). These techniques are based on Lorentz force to achieve the required goal. The force is generated when a high voltage charged capacitor bank discharge through a forming/displacement coil placed in the proximity of work piece. The force developed is on account of interaction of induced current in the work piece with the magnetic field produced by the coil. In these techniques, forming and welding are achieved without physical contact between tool and job piece. Hence, it has obvious merits over conventional process such as brazing, welding, expansion, contraction, contour formation etc. This sophisticated technique has many advantages such as precision, reproducibility, high production rate, no tool mark, minimization of manual error, automation ease etc. The preparatory procedures such has preheating, lubricating etc. are not needed. Since the bond is achieved by impact/pressure, this method is ideally suited for joining/welding of dissimilar metals with large difference in their melting points. This added advantage is generally not available in the conventional processes. This technique has applicable in automobile, electric, defence, aeronautical and other industries. It has tremendous potential for use in the manufacture of appliances and consumer products. For the sake of Convenience, the system is configured into various Racks. Rack-1 consists of Capacitor Charging Power Supply, Programmable Logic Controller & dump resistor unit. Rack-2 comprises Discharge capacitor Bank and the working table consists of EMM Tool. In addition, HMI and Oscilloscope is provided for system operation and recording waveforms. The multi stage Marx Generator is charged via an external power supply to the desired voltage. When fully charged Marx generator discharges rapidly into the electron accelerator tube creating a large potential difference across the diode gap. The cathode consists of a stainless steel disc which readily emits electrons when the high voltage is applied. The anode is a tungsten rod placed coaxial with the cathode disc. The electrons are accelerated across the anode-cathode spacing until they impact with the anode rod target. The resulting bremsstrahlung process produces the desired radiation. The charging and discharging phases of the operation are controlled through a PLC based control system. FXR machines are designed to give extremely short duration (sub-microsecond) and extremely intense bursts of x-ray radiation. These sources have higher radiation power than continuously emitting conventional x-ray tubes which makes them useful for the investigation of non-transparent high speed transient phenomena. The FXR system can see through smoke and fire to reveal how a projectile or weapon interacts with armour at the exact moment of impact. FXR systems provide a unique method of imaging very fast events, which cannot be captured utilizing normal high speed and ultra-high speed photographic techniques. This is a highly sophisticated accelerator complex which will provide high-energy, precisely-tailored beams of antiprotons and many kinds of ions. These charged particle beams will then be accelerated and employed to create new, often highly exotic particles in a series of parallel experimental programmes. This is developed under international consortium for the particle physics experiments. FAIR is being built through international collaboration and India is a major partner. Other contributing nations include Austria, China, Finland, France, Germany, Great Britain, Greece, Italy, Poland, Romania, Russia, Slovenia, Slovakia, Spain & Sweden. These will power the super conducting and normal conducting Magnets that bend the high energy particle beams. The Power Converters consists of any one of the three configurations (1 Quadrant, 2 Quadrant or 4 Quadrant) using switched mode structure (Hard switching). The three phase input voltage is stepped down by a three phase Delta/star or Delta/delta transformer and then rectified by full wave three phase diode bridge followed by an LC filter. DC link voltage is fed to the IGBT based switch-mode converter circuit followed by output LC filter, damping resistor, damping capacitor and load circuit. Output current is sensed and compared with the set value to generate the control signal for IGBT. Controller selects the IGBTs for switching. Controller adjusts the PWM duty cycle in order to get the required output. Nominal switching frequency of each IGBT is 10 kHz and the resulting output frequency is 20 kHz. tags: BARCIS INSERVICE UNDERWATER INSPECTION HEADS (UIH) for NPPs
content: The operation of Pressurized Heavy Water Reactors (PHWRs) are based on the use of natural Uranium fuel, heavy water as moderator and pressure tube (PT) as containment for primary coolant, fuel bundles and “ON POWER” re-fuelling. Due to the critically important role of the pressure tube (PT) as a part of pressure boundary, it is necessary to confirm their structural integrity and collect data related to changes in their metallurgical properties, geometry and condition in order to predict the service life (healthiness) of the PT. In PHWRs, In-service inspection of PT is done to ensure its healthiness for the smooth and safe operation of NPPs. The Underwater Inspection Head (UIH) moves inside PT for the measurement of different parameters like PT Wall thickness, Inside Diameter, Axial and Circumferential Flaws, Sag etc. UIH carries the Ultrasonic and Eddy Current probes for the measurement of these parameters. Before introduction of UIH in PT, the Inspection Head’s Ultrasonic and Eddy Current Probes needs to be calibrated to the required measuring parameters and check of healthiness of these Probes. ECIL also manufactures the Calibration Facility to carry out the calibration of Probes. ECIL currently manufactures two variants of UIHs and Calibration Facility for NPPs across India. UIH for 220 MWe PHWRs; UIH for 540/700 MWe PHWRs. Calibration Facility for UIH for 220 MWe PHWRs.; Calibration Facility for UIH for 540/700 MWe PHWRs. It is an advanced Command Control Computer Communication and Intelligence (C4I) architecture for precise and effective engagement of weapons against moving targets. The heart of the weapon complex is the Command & Control Centre, which is capable of (tasking) communicating to 3D-CAR and four Troop Control Centre (TCC)for execution of Missile Launch. CCC can also serve as the nerve centre for interoperability with other weapon systems located in the base. Secured communication through communication media with encryption mechanism is used for communication between CCC, 3D-Central Acquisition Radar(3D-CAR) and TCC for weapon engagement. content: BRAHMOS Missile operates on ‘Fire and Forget' principle, adopting varieties of flight paths on its way to the target. The missile's destructive power is enhanced due to the large kinetic energy on impact. ECIL provides the Ground Support Equipment (GSE) to Brahmos Weapon Complex System comprising of Mobile Autonomous Launchers (MALs), Mobile Command Post (MCP) and Light Combat Support Vehicle (LCSV). Strategic Electronics Division (SED), ECIL is the prime integrator of Brahmos Weapon Complex System. MCP is state-of-the-art mobile command post realized in an NBC protected self-sufficient shelter on a TATRA 8X8 vehicle containing an equipment shelter and a DG shelter, auto level-controlled jacks and other associated equipment. MCP provides target data with instruction to each MAL for engaging specific target. MCP assists in integrating the MAL into the net centric warfare. The main role of MCP is planning the mission identiﬁcation of suitable MAL for effective neutralization of target and issue of launch order to MALs, secure and reliable communication with the connected entities, data recording and analysis. System design realized meeting all the required environmental Specifications as per JSS55555 and EMI/EMC as per MIL-STD-461E. MAL is a weapon launcher that consists of three missiles in ready to launch configuration with most modern means of communication. The missile can be fired in single or salvo of 2 to 3 within four minutes of receiving command depending on the command received from MCP. It can fire towards single or three different targets. The Mobile Autonomous Launcher (MAL) is capable of receiving the target information from Mobile Command Post (MCP) and provides an interface to the Fire Control System. MAL is realized in a NBC and EMI / EMC protected self-contained shelter. This facilitates ﬁring of missiles against targets. LCSV is an entity located at nearest user location for providing the necessary information to support the combat activities. The Light Combat Support Vehicle (LCSV) is fitted with communication equipment to establish communication with MCP. The vehicles are modified to carry radio equipment, additional fuel, personal baggage and mountable GPS receiver for road navigation. Brahmos Training Simulator is developed for classroom training for proper understanding, training, learning and operations about MCP, MAL, LCSV of Brahmos Missile System (BMS). title: Crypto Products | ECIL | DAE | India
tags: Encryption Product for Two Way Analog/ Digital Radios (for MOTOROLA)
content: Security of information plays major role now a days to communicate confidential information. With increased security threats, standard encryption algorithms emerged to provide security solutions. But, these solutions provide limited security. ECIL has played a vital role in providing effective security solutions with in house development of algorithms. These Encryption products are designed as per CPC Guidelines to meet Scientific Analysis Group (SAG) grading requirements. Key Management is designed keeping in view of the JCB requirements. ECIL has obtained SAG grading from G2 to G4 for different types of equipments. The ECIL’s ENCRYPTION product is designed to make the Two way Radio communication secure. ECIL has developed this product for both Analog version (GP-338/ GM-338) and also for Digital version Moto Turbo versions of Motorola made radios. The Analog version was SAG approved and is supplied to Military and Paramilitary forces for the past 10 years. Digital version was field trailed and is ready for SAG approval. modules are gracefully fit inside the Radios. Multiport Encryption Line Interface Crypto (MELIC) is developed to provide Secure digital Encryption of voice, data and fax over PSTN, Army owned ASCON, AREN and Satellite Networks. The unit resembles the normal telephone by providing all its features and in addition to that it also performs encryption. MELIC, a digital encryption device, provides Confidentiality, Integrity and Authenticity to the Information. The device supports Clear( Un-encrypted) and secure (Encrypted) mode of operations. MELIC supports variable data baud rates from 2.4Kbps to 38.4 Kbps for secure data and supports G3 Fax Protocols with variable baud rates from 2.4K to 14.4K. In addition to that it has a facility to accept secure fax call and store secure fax information in the absence of user. Auto fax is password protected and only authorized persons can print from stored secure fax information. Radio Interface Encryption Device (RIED) is available as a standalone model for being used for secure communication between Ground to Ground / Ground to Air Half Duplex Radio Communication over VHF/ UHF and HF Radios. The Encryption unit works from 230V or 28V supplied by Aircraft and has required power conversion circuits for facilitating such operations. Ground to Ground / Air to Air Encryption Equipment - RIED is designed to provide encryption or encryption for Voice communication between Ground to Ground / Ground to Air Communication HF/VHF/UHF Radios. A high speed Digital signal processor provides high level secured encryption/ decryption and performs necessary control operations. The Ground to Ground / Ground to Air Encryption Equipment - RIED uses latest state of the art technology. Gautam Encryption Unit is designed to provide encryption/ decryption for messages / File sent / receive from terminal PC. A high speed Digital Signal Processor provides high level secured encryption/ decryption and performs necessary control operations. This Unit will detect automatically from the input message for Encryption or Decryption. The data received from the data port connected to the PC is analyzed for Authentication, Encryption/ Decryption and processed. The Key information is stored in a non-volatile memory block. The key memory block is password protected and key can be erased in case of emergency using password followed by command. File Encryption Module (FEM) is designed to provide encryption/ decryption for messages/ files send/ receive from terminal PC/ Laptop. A high speed Digital Signal Processor provides high level secured encryption/ decryption by in-house developed proprietary algorithm and performs necessary control operations. This Unit will detect automatically from the input message for Encryption/ Decryption. The data received from the data port connected to the PC/ Laptop is analyzed for Offline File/ Message Encryptor/ Decryptor Authentication, Encryption/ Decryption and processed. The Key information is stored in a non-volatile memory block. The E1 Encryption Unit is used for encrypting the E1 links between the two locations. The interface characteristics are as per G.703 , support framing and alarms as per G.704. This equipment also supports unframed modes of operations. The equipment is ported with Indigenously developed Algorithm and supports key management system as per CPC Guidelines. The equipment is available in both Single E1 interface (1U Height) and also Multi interface, 4 or 8 E1 Interface in 5U height with redundant Power supplies and Control Units. The equipment supports SNMP and configurable for V2c and V3. The Ethernet Encryption Unit is used for encrypting the IP network between the two locations. The interface characteristics are as per IEEE 802.3. This equipment supports 10/10/1000 Mbps both Electrical (RJ-45) and Optical Interafce(SFP). This equipment also supports both Tunnel and Transport modes of operations. The equipment is ported with indigenously developed Algorithm and supports key management system as per CPC Guidelines. The STM1/4 Encryption Unit is used for encrypting the STM 1/4 links between the two locations. The interface characteristics are as per ITU-T G.707, ITU-T G.957, ITU-T G.783. The equipment supports framing as per G.707. The equipment is ported with indigenously developed Algorithm and supports key management system as poer CPC guidelines. The Next Generation Bulk Encryption Unit (NGBEU) or Multi Capacity Encryption Unit(MCEU) is used for encrypting the data links in the network either point to point or Point to Multi Point. This equipment supports interfaces from n*64Kbps to 10Gbps with different physical interfaces that support different data rates with universal motherboard. Some of the Tributary card can be configured for more than one data rate from the front panel keyboard. This equipment is very versatile and supports NMS with SNMP ver 2C/ ver 3 Protocol. The equipment is ported with indigenously developed Algorithm and supports key management system as per CPC guidelines. title: Electronic Fuzes for Artillery Ammunition | ECIL | DAE | India
content: ECIL has been a primary supplier of Electronic Fuzes to the Indian Army for the past 25 years, delivering over 2.2 million units to the Ministry of Defence. These Fuzes, provided by ECIL, boast a reliability rate exceeding 95% and are engineered to operate effectively across all terrains and weather conditions. They are compatible with 105mm, 130mm, and 155mm artillery shells and are used for initiating the explosive sequence of Artillery Ammunition. ECIL produces three types of Electronic Fuzes within the “M85P13” series: The classification of the Fuzes produced against each variant of the gun is tabulated as below: ECIL also provides the Fuze Setter (M15), a device used to configure the functional mode and read the settings of Proximity and Time Fuzes prior to their use with artillery ammunition. The M85P13PD series Electronic Percussion Fuze, also referred to as a point-detonating Fuze, activates upon impact. The Fuze initiates the explosive sequence within the artillery ammunition. It is primarily used with High-Explosive Shells against targets such as personnel, convoys, buildings, light vehicles, and similar threats. The M85P13A series electronic proximity Fuze is specifically designed to detonate approximately 10 ± 6 meters above the target. It utilizes an RF transceiver to measure altitude during the Flight path, after firing from the gun. Additionally, it includes a Point Detonation (PD) mode for instant detonation upon impact. The mode and Electronic Counter-Counter Measures (ECCM) settings are configured using the Fuze Setter (M15). This Fuze is used with high-explosive shells targeting personnel, convoys and troop movements, offering a lethality area up to 10 times greater than that of a Point Detonation (PD) Fuze. The M85P13T series Electronic Time Fuze is primarily designed to detonate at SET time. It initiates the explosive sequence within artillery ammunition via an electronic firing circuit at the SET time. Additionally, it features a Point Detonation (PD) mode for immediate detonation upon impact. Both the mode and the timing are configured using the Fuze Setter (M15). This Fuze is commonly used with carrier shells such as illumination, cargo, and smoke shells. The Fuze Setter (M15) is a handheld electronic inductive device, manufactured by ECIL, for programming and reading Proximity and Time Fuzes. These inductive setters select operating modes for both Proximity and Time Fuzes for setting the detonation interval for Time Fuzes, and program the RF inhibition interval in Proximity Fuzes to enable ECCM functionality. content: Electronics Corporation of India Limited, a Government of India Enterprise under Department of Atomic Energy, has been supporting country’s space program right from inception by setting up the ground antenna network at all centers of Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) for communication. It is proud to be associated with the Chandrayaan-3 Mission by way of providing the indigenously designed antenna systems needed for Tracking, Telemetry, Command and Ranging (TTC&R) operations of moon mission program through ISRO Telemetry Tracking and Command Network (ISTRAC). ECIL supplied the 32-meter-Deep Space Network (DSN) antenna which facilitated the vital communication support for Chandrayaan mission. This 300ton Antenna System has been built indigenously in association with Bhabha Atomic Research Center (BARC), U R Rao Satellite Centre (URSC) and ISTRAC. The antennae precisely points to the spacecraft orbiting around moon at about 4 lakh KM distance from earth for command-and-control operations. The Antenna System employs state-of-the-art technology of precision formed reflector surface with an accuracy better than 0.3 millimeters, Wheel and Track Mount, Beam Wave guide, Feed Systems and Servo Control System. The realization of this Antenna involved almost all the disciplines of engineering like soil mechanics, Structural Engineering, Mechanical, Radio Frequency & Microwave and Control Engineering. It will continue to play crucial role during acquisition of data and images from moon captured by Vikram and Pragyan. ECIL also provided 18,11 and 7.2-meter Antenna systems and 4.5-meter Ship borne Terminal to ISTRAC to support tracking, telemetry and command operations of space mission critical programs right from the time of launch. Communication with spacecraft plays a vital role in various space missions and Aditya L1 mission of Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) is no exception. The antenna systems on the spacecraft and ground facilitate the communication. Electronics Corporation of India Limited (ECIL), a Government of India Enterprise under Department of Atomic Energy, is supporting Aditya mission by setting up the ground station antenna network for communication. The indigenous 18-meter antenna set up by ECIL at Bylalu village at about 40kms distance from Bangaluru plays a significant role in the communication system of Aditya mission.This first of its kind monopulse earth station antenna is designed, developed, manufactured and commissioned by ECIL in association with BARC and ISRO. The Antenna System employs state-of-the-art technology to precisely point at the spacecraft orbiting around sun at about 15 lakh kilometers distance from earth for acquisition of data and videos. This earth station antenna is an integral part of Indian Deep Space Network (IDSN) established for facilitating interplanetary communications. The 32 meter Deep Space Network antenna supplied by ECIL earlier is also part of ISDN. In addition to them, ECIL also provided 11meter Antenna systems to ISRO for supporting the tracking, telemetry. ECIL with the technical support of BARC has played a pivotal role in advancing nuclear technology for FBR by supplying precise Control and Instrumentation (C&I) systems for the Prototype Fast Breeder Reactor (PFBR) at Kalpakkam. Multi-Mode Radar (MMR) is a vital weapon component of a fighter aircraft such as India’s Light Combat Aircraft (LCA) TEJAS. It is a versatile instrument supporting various modes such as target search, track-while-scan, single target track and multiple target track. The Antenna PLatform (APL) is an electromechanical subsystem of the MMR with a two axis gimbal mechanism and position servo with Mil-Std-1553B interface to the Radar Processor (RP). APL positions the flat plate antenna so as to point the RF beam in the desired direction. The MACE telescope is the second-largest gamma ray telescope in the world and will help the scientific community enhance its understanding in the fields of astrophysics, fundamental physics, and particle acceleration mechanisms. The MACE Telescope consists of a large-area tessellated light collector of 356 m², made up of 356 mirror panels. A high-resolution imaging camera weighing about 1200 kg, for detection and characterization of the atmospheric Cherenkov events, forms the focal plane instrumentation of the telescope. The elevation over azimuth mounted telescope basket structure has two axes movement capability of ± 270° in azimuth and -26° to +165° in elevation for pointing towards any source in the sky and tracking it. The telescope, which weighs about 180 tons, is supported on six wheels which move on a 27-metre-diameter track. The telescope has an integrated imaging camera, which contains 1088 photo multiplier-based pixels and all the signal processing and data acquisition electronics. The camera communicates the acquired data to the computer system in the control room over optical fiber. An ECIL fabricated antenna system has been installed in India’s base station on the icy continent of Antarctica. The project links Bharti Station to NRSC, Shadnagar. The link also provides a two-way communication service between Antarctica and NCAOR (National Centre for Antarctica and Ocean Research) Goa which is the nodal agency for the coordination and implementation of Indian Antarctica Support programme. In 2007, ECIL established the communication link between Maitri Station in Antarctica and NCAOR for providing communication link between the station and mainland India. content: ECIL is India's preferred supplier of Antenna products and SATCOM systems ranging from suitcase terminals to mammoth 300 ton structures. Backed by a vibrant R&D program, ECIL has built-up a valuable product development and manufacturing capability encompassing civil, mechanical, control, RF and network domains. ECIL has done pioneering work in the design and development of large antennas like the 2m diameter IDSN antenna for the country’s 1st Lunar Mission, Chandrayaan-I. After the successful commissioning of this antenna the challenging task of design and manufacture of the Gamma Ray Telescope, MACE was taken up. The detailed engineering design was developed from a conceptual science design. As part of the detailed design the structure of the telescope was optimized and its weight was reduced from 220 tonnes to 180 tonnes. In view of the arid cold conditions prevailing at Hanle, special attention was given to the selection of all the materials required for the fabrication of the telescope. Development of diamond turned metallic mirrors was initiated in the country and about 1500 honeycomb based aluminium mirrors have been manufactured to the stringent accuracies required for the telescope. Precision actuators which can control the movement of the individual mirror panels with an accuracy of 10 microns have been developed indigenously. The dual Drive System for both Azimuth & Elevation axes of the telescope has been designed to take care of its operational requirement of fast slewing and tracking movement. Operating at a slewing speed of 2.4 deg/sec. the telescope can point to any direction in the sky within 75 seconds. The Drive system employs in-line Gear Boxes with single servo motor input and electromagnetic gear changing mechanism to accomplish precise pointing accuracy of less than 16 milli degrees. The entire structure has been designed and fabricated with high stiffness to meet the natural frequency requirement of more than 1 Hz. 1088 pixel photomultiplier tube based imaging camera which will take the snap-shot of the few nano second duration Cherenkov event generated by an incident VHE gamma-ray photon is being realized at ECIL. The 2m x 2m x 1.25m camera will use about 700 PCBs of 10 different types. More than 25 engineers and technicians of ECIL have been associated with the development of the telescope for the last few years. Similar telescopes like H.E.S.S, MAGIC and VERITAS setup in Namibia, Europe and US respectively have been realized by multi-national collaborative efforts of multiple institutions. The MACE telescope has been designed and realized from concept stage to trial assembly stage by ECIL, with technology support from BARC. A number of major private organizations have also contributed to the development of various sub-systems of the telescope like Wheel & Track Assembly, Gear Box Assembly, multi-segment Elevation Bull Gear, Elevation Plummer block, metallic mirrors etc. After successful conclusion of the trial assembly of the telescope at Hyderabad the disassembly, transportation to Hanle and its installation there will be taken up. The commissioning trials at Hanle will be started towards the end of 2015 and the telescope will be fully operational by the summer of 2016. The 21m diameter MACE telescope will be the second largest gamma-ray telescope in the world and will operate at the same trigger threshold of about 30GeV as the 28m diameter HESS telescope operating in Namibia. content: ECIL has provided the Integrated Security Solutions to provide proactive,preventive and protective security to the VIPs/ VVIPs, building and its incumbents. It includes access control and regulation of people, material and vehicles within the historical and prestigious Parliament House Complex including but not limited to PM’s Office and PM’s Residence and Delhi Secretariat & UP Vidhan Sabha. In today’s world, devices such as Mobile phones, Drones, COTS Remote Control Units, FM/ Citizen Frequency Band Radios etc. can be used to trigger RCIEDs. To mitigate this threat Vehicle Mounted Jammers (VMJs), generally referred to as convey jammers were supplied to Delhi Police by ECIL. content: Automatic Message Switching System is a proven and time tested ECIL's IP based state-of-art integrated message switching solution to cater Air Traffic Control Services on AFTN network and is based on COTS hardware. The system operates on the store and forward principle and is in accordance with ICAO recommendations and industry standard practices. The AMSS switch architecture is fault tolerant working in High availability mode. Modular design of the AMSS allows easy extension of the base system as per needs. AMSS supports various line types such as RS232, E-mail, X.25, Mini-AMSS, TCP/IP etc. and it can be configured flexibly in terms of processing capacity and supported line types. AMSS user interface is web based and is easy to use. User positions can be connected through LAN, MPLS or Internet. In terms of security, the system uses two levels of authentication (User and Role), which corresponds to a specific Application. Based on Application & Role, system allows the user to NOTAM, ATS(FPL, DEP, ARR etc.), MET, HFRT and other AFTN messages compilation. Supervisory role provides control and supervision of the system. System also provides additional functionalities like ADC/ FIC/ YA/ Area workflow, RPL management and YA automation. title: Jammer Products | ECIL | DAE | India
content: ECIL has fathomless and canned expertise in RF Jamming technique which is acquired through immense projects execution. Core-Expertise in RF Jammers is an aftermath due to decades of immortal discussions with our esteemed Customers. ECIL has supplied diverse Jammer products like RCIED Jammers, Cell Phone Jammers, Convoy Jammers etc. to State POLICE, Paramilitary and Defense forces as an extension to Home-Land Security Systems. Vehicle Mounted Jammer is a state of art system used to counter Remote Controlled Improvised Explosive Devices (RCIED) and Cell Phone bands in the frequency range of 20-6000 MHz. The system is usually mounted on SUV with provision to use additional Alternator as a Power Source to Jammer System which is fitted in the Vehicle. Electrical backup of upto 30 Minutes is also featured. The system has capacity to Jam the frequency bands of HF, VHF, UHF, Cell phones (2G,3G,4G,5G), WIFI, Bluetooth and Drone bands. The system is modular with dedicated Exciter, Power Amplifier and Transmitting Antenna. Vehicle Mounted Jammers are marketed with the Model : ECSVJEE - 1100U (Capable to provide Jamming upto 5G mobile, RCIED, Wifi and Drone frequencies) EC-SJJE-200 is designed to restrict the use of cell phone in a designated area.The bands of GSM, EGSM, 3-G, 4-G & CDMA are jammed in vicinity of 75 meters using EC-SJJE-200M1. EC-SJJE-200M1 has a modular design and it consists of independent transmitting (jamming) channels (modules). Each independent transmitting module generates barrage jamming with frequency according to cellphone bandwidth. The system is equipped with status indicators and protection features from Overheating, High VSWR and Reverse Polarity. Depending upon the application Omnidirectional/Directional antennae are deployed with the system. The system operates on 220 V AC and also has the provision of battery backup. Cellphone Jammers are marketed with the Model : EC-SJJE-200M1 (For Establishments and Prisons) The Portable RCIED Jammer EC-SPJE-400 is a state of the art Electronic Counter Measure System designed & developed as a Counter Measure against any kind of RCIED attack by the Militant Groups or Terrorist Outfits. It mutes the remotely Controlled Devices which would be used by the Militant Groups to detonate the bombs. The system has total 7 Bands comprising of seven individual antennas. All the antennas are Omni-directional for providing uniform coverage. The system is designed from 20-500 MHz, which is sub-divided into three bands & each band has power output of 80 watts approximately. Further the system has four work bands i.e. CDMA (800-900 MHz), GSM-I (900-1000 MHz), GSM II (1800-1900 MHz) & 3G (2100-2200 MHz). Each band has been given O/p power of 40W for providing suitable jamming all around as required. The system comes with a felicitous Pelican Case The system is designed for use during the movement of the VVIP’s, Movement of the Troops & even during the search & rescue operations by the Bomb Disposal Team. Portable RCIED Jammers are marketed with the Model : EC-SPJE-400 The Manpack Jammer EC-SMJ-30 is intended for protection against Radio Remote Controlled Improvised Explosive Devices (RCIED). EC-SMJ-30 is used for protection of single person or group of people against RCIED. EC-SMJ-30 has a modular design and it consists of a single transmitting module. content: Electronic Voting Machines (EVMs) have strengthened India’s electoral system since their initial introduction in 1999 and universal deployment from 2004. Designed to replace paper ballots, EVMs deliver speed, accuracy, transparency, and tamper-resistant operation in every phase of the election process. Each EVM includes a unique laser-marked serial number, highly secure communication protocols, and interfaces for accessories such as VVPAT, FLCU, PADU, Totalizer, and Printing Units. Critical features like real-time clock, time stamping, event logging, and Power-ON self-diagnostics ensure that only healthy and genuine units are used in the field. All connected units authenticate each other at startup, preventing unauthorized or mismatched devices. The Ballot Unit supports Braille labels for visually challenged voters, and the EVM system integrates seamlessly with VVPAT for enhanced transparency and verifiability. VVPAT enables voters to verify their selection through a printed slip that is automatically cut and stored in a sealed compartment, ensuring transparency while protecting voter privacy. The VVPAT operates on battery power for easy portability and has a capacity to store 1,500 Ballot slips. VVPAT performs its health diagnostics every power on. It includes secure sealing provisions and features LASER-marked unique serial numbers on its cabinets for reliable identification and tamper-resistance. The Multi-Post Multi-Vote Electronic Voting Machine (EVM). It integrates advanced capabilities for security, verifiability, and traceability, designed specifically to meet the requirements of local body elections for State Election Commission(SEC) involving multiple posts and seats. This versatile configuration supports complex ballot structures, offering greater efficiency, flexibility, and transparency during elections. content: Software-defined Wide Area Network (SD-WAN) is a virtual WAN architecture, communicating using overlay tunnels along with security encryption technique and abstracting the software from the hardware for centralized control. SD-WAN simplify the IT infrastructure deployment, control and management of services. The Metro Ethernet Forum (MEF) has defined an SD-WAN architecture consisting of an SD-WAN edge, SD-WAN gateway, SD-WAN controller and SD-WAN orchestrator. Portable Radioisotope Identifier Device (PRID) is a field-deployable gamma spectrometry system designed for rapid detection, localization, quantification, and isotopic identification of radioactive materials. Surface Wave Over the Horizon Radar is a multi-sensor, HF-band maritime and airborne surveillance antenna system that ensures the detection of surface targets and low flying airborne threats which is not possible from microwave radar.(SWOTHR) is a cost-effective in terms of both operation and maintenance compared to ground based, ship borne or air borne sensors as surveillance area range is restricted due to Line of Sight (LoS) and high operational cost. These sensors will be operated in High Frequency band. It detects surface targets and low-flying airborne threats. ECIL has engineered and manufactured BARC indigenously developed dry calorimeter for the strategic needs of the nuclear facilities and supplied to customers. This is an important technological achievement and a shining example of BARC - ECIL collaboration towards self-reliance. Calorimeter measures heat energy transfer due to temperature differences. Radiometric calorimeter operates on the principle that the radioactive decay of all isotopes generates heat and almost all of the energy associated with the decay of radioactive materials placed in the sample chamber is absorbed in the form of heat within the calorimeter. Thus the calorimeter is an accurate, non-destructive technique for testing Special Nuclear Materials (SNM). The heat output of the SNM sample is directly proportional to the quantity of radioactive material present in the sample. content: ECIL is proud to manufacture Electronic Systems, Mass Manufacturing of PCBs etc. using the well-established Secure Manufacturing Facilities (SMF) at EMSD. ECIL has proven track record of supplying EVMs, VVPATs to Central Government & various State Governments, Local Bodies etc., from the last two decades. Electronic Manufacturing Services Division (EMSD) of ECIL deals in Mass Manufacturing of Electronic Products and population of High Density Complex PCB Assemblies. EMSD has been in the business of Electronic Voting Machines (EVMs) for Election Commission of India (ECI) and State Election Commissions (SECs) of different States in India for over a decade. EMSD has the credit of manufacturing 8,50,000 EVMs and supplying them to ECI and SECs. These machines were successfully used in the general Elections of 2004 and 2009, 2014, 2019 both for Assembly and Parliament. In addition, this Division has undertaken the production of 2,50,000 PCB Assemblies consisting of SMT and leaded components for single phase Static Electronic Energy Meter and supplied to different electricity boards in the Country. We also, deal in supplying very complex multiple layer PCB assemblies for DAE projects of NPCIL, PFBR and other customers . We meet the requirement of DAE of their very high standard of stage wise quality inspections including Optical and X-Ray for the 100% quality and met all the stringent relevant quality standards of manufacturers. Therefore, to sum up the entire capability of our Division, that we have all the qualifications of being the mass manufacturer of any electronic product, mass population of any kind of PCBs consisting of SMT devices, leaded components etc., Turnkey conversion into electronic product i.e., with the supply of manufacturing documents, we can procure all the components like Electronic (passive, active, SMT etc.,) Mechanical, Electro Mechanical, Plastic Parts etc., and convert them in to finished products, test as per the ATPs and supply them to customers at their destinations. As far as the infrastructure of our Division is concerned, all the technical data of each and every machine is provided to the benefit of our prospective customers who can understand our capability well and approaching us for their mass requirement of either for the complete product conversion or a part of it like the electronic population of any type of complex (multi-layer) PCBs including testing. ECIL has put in place a secure manufacturing facility for production of Electronic Voting Machines (EVM) and Voter Verifiable Paper Audit Trial (VVPAT). The secure manufacturing software provides security and also allows traceability of the EVM and VVPAT units up to component level, which would help in preventing security breaches, theft, and misuse of EVMs, VVPATs as well as disruption or denial of services. All the stages and the activities are monitored and logged using the secure manufacturing software. The software provides for Recording of SMT components being loaded, tracking of PCBs, Traceability up to components level, recording of manufacturing information data relating to the EVM & VVPAT units from PCB stage to the final quality control, packing and shipment of the units. The data recording includes the activities carried out, operation status, unit/ sub unit ID and the stage at which operation has been carried out, Operator ID, Date & Time of operation Display of production status at each stage of manufacturing and Generation of Alerts in case of operational errors, time delays, improper operating sequence. The secure manufacturing software is successfully implemented at the Election Equipment Manufacturing Facility. EMS 2.0 is a cloud-native application designed & developed for Inventory Management of EVMs & VVPATs across all 36 States & UTs and Manufacturers. In 1977 the Chief Election Commissioner requested ECIL to design a machine that suits the Indian election procedures in order to promote e-voting. Subsequently in 1979, ECIL developed a prototype and submitted to ECI which was used for the first time in 50 polling stations of Parur Constituency of Kerala in 1982. But due to the absence of a specific law prescribing the use of EVM led the Supreme Court to strike down those elections. Later through article 61A Representative of Peoples Act was amended that empowered ECI to bring EVMs into force during the elections. Henceforth ECI procured 75,000 EVMs during November 1989 to March 1990. It was in 2004 General Elections to Lok Sabha that EVMs were used in all the 543 Polling Constituencies thus replacing the erstwhile usage of ballot papers in-toto. These EVMs were called 'M1 EVMs' since these were upgraded in 2006 and were termed 'M2 EVMs'. These are further upgraded as 'M3 EVMs' in 2013. There was a request in an all political meet in October 2010 to introduce more transparency and verifiability in the polling process and as a result, on the advice of TEC, ECIL and BEL developed a prototype that was demonstrated in 2011 for which simulated election for the field trials of the VVPAT (Voter Verified Paper Audit Trial) were conducted in various states and eventually VVPATs were used for the first time in September 2013 in bye-election in Nagaland. Since 2000, EVMs have been used in all 3 Lok Sabha and 118 State Legislative Assemblies' elections. title: Environmental & Durability Test Laboratory (EDTL) | ECIL | DAE | India
content: Environmental & Durability Test Laboratory (EDTL) facilitates the evaluation of the performance of products operating in extreme environmental conditions of Temperature, Humidity, Pressure, Corrosion and Vibration etc. EDTL facility is primarily located in Systems and Quality Assurance Group (SQAG) at ECIL Hyderabad Factory which is a Corporate Service Provider in all areas of Quality, Reliability and Industrial Engineering relevant to Electronics and IT Industry. The state of art Environmental Test Laboratory (ETL) facility includes latest environmental test chambers and equipment’s such as Thermal Shock Chamber, Combined Altitude Temperature & Humidity (CATH) Chamber, Highly Accelerated Life Testing/Highly Accelerated Stress Screening (HALT/HASS) Chamber, Environmental Stress Screening (ESS)Chambers, Salt Spray Chamber, Dust Chamber, Rain Chamber, Ingression Protection(IP) against dust and water test facilities etc., These chambers and machines are used for climatic testing, screening of electronic components, process qualification related testing and Aging/Stress reliving of fabricated parts as per the standards JSS 55555, IEC, IS, MIL, QM-333 etc., The Durability Test Laboratory (DTL) provides various durability tests to ensure the performance of the product under extreme mechanical stress. These tests ensure that the product can withstand various types of mechanical failures such as cracking, deformation, breaking, loosening etc., encountered in the real environment. Durability Test Laboratory has facilities for Vibration Test, Bump Test, Impact (K-200) Test, Drop Test, Shock Test, Jolt and Jumble test, Toppling Test. Application of these tests are found in many branches of engineering, such as aerospace, civil, mechanical, mechatronics and even electrical and electronics. Monitoring and testing of vibrations and experiments are important in the design, implementation, maintenance and repair of engineering systems. Apart from meeting internal testing requirements, the facilities are utilized by external organizations on chargeable basis. EDTL, a world-class test facility always welcomes the opportunity to understand and fulfil customer’s testing requirements. Please feel free to contact us for any testing related information. content: Calibration & Measurements Laboratory (CML) is a state-of-the-art calibration facility that ensures the reliability of products and processes by accurately calibrating the instruments that are used to measure critical parameters. CML facility is housed in Systems and Quality Assurance Group (SQAG) at ECIL Hyderabad which is a Corporate Service Provider in all areas of Quality, Reliability and Industrial Engineering relevant to Electronics and IT Industry. The calibration lab is accredited to NABL as per ISO/IEC 17025: 2017. Facilities are available to calibrate parameters like voltage (AC&DC), current (AC&DC), resistance, capacitance, inductance, frequency, Bandwidth, Acceleration, Temperature & Humidity, RF power etc. of instruments to ensure satisfactory performance. The laboratory offers calibration services for measurement of various test instruments including Accelerometers, Multimeters up to 8½ digit, Oscilloscopes, Clamp meters, Power meters, Current, Voltage sources, LCR meters and Hand held calibrators etc. Our well-maintained infrastructure and experienced team guarantee accurate & reliable results for all the equipment. Plans are on the anvil to augment the existing infrastructure and enhance the scope of the LAB. The facilities can be utilized by all organizations on charged basis. If you require any additional information please feel free to contact us. title: EMI/EMC Test Facility (ETF) | ECIL | DAE | India
content: A state-of-the-art EMI/EMC Test and measurement Facility has been set up in Electronics Corporation of India Limited, Hyderabad to support Electromagnetic Interference/ Compatibility conformal testing of Electronic Products. The facility is strategically located and meets the testing requirements of many customers throughout the country. The testing labs are equipped with world class equipment to test electronic products for applications in the Nuclear, Defence, Space, Telecom, Railways, Medical, Consumer Electronics and other important sectors in the areas of Strategic Electronics. Electronic systems can be subjected to testing and certification across a wide range of global standards, such as MIL-STD-461 E/F/G, IEC/EN Standards, CISPR Standards etc. With the view to serve the requirements of the chosen sector, ETF has set up infrastructure comprising of 10-meter Semi Anechoic Chamber with integrated 4 meter turntable having a load bearing capacity of 5 tons. Sheltered vehicles weighing up to 30 ton with an axle weight up to 12 tonnes can be accommodated inside the chamber. In addition to this, there are labs for Bulk cable Injection, Conducted RF, Transient, Common Mode Disturbance and Power Quality Testing. Shielding Effectiveness tests for shelters with minimum dimension greater than 2m are also conducted as per IEEE 299. The test facility is accredited by NABL as per ISO/IEC 17025:2017 standard and designated by TEC as Conformity Assessment Body (CAB) for the mandatory testing of telecommunication equipment. The facility offers full-compliance development testing services, where the customers can carry out iterative tests and troubleshoot failures to rectify any design issues. The lab shares the raw test results, so that the customers can review the data, identify the root cause and meet the requirements of the standards. Additionally the facility offers full-compliance certification services, where the unit is subjected to the tests as per customer requirements. Accredited test reports are subsequently provided which help the customers achieve their compliance goals nationally and internationally. title: Compact Antenna Test Range Facility (CATF) | ECIL | DAE | India
content: The COMPACT Antenna Test Range Facility established at ECIL is capable of measuring all the essential parameters of antennas in the frequency band of 1.0GHz to 40GHz which can be extended upto 100GHz on demand. The facility consists of a shielded anechoic chamber, Modular in construction, providing a shielding of 80dB typical up to 40GHz. The Size of the Chamber is 10.5mW) x 10.5m (H) x 18.4m (L) to fit in to an empty room size of 15.6m(W) x 12.5 (H) x 21.4m (L). The facility includes rolled edge corner fed reflector system, providing 2.4m (H) x 2.4m (W) x 2.4m (L) minimum size of quiet zone, Feed Positioner carousel for simultaneous mounting of up to 4 feeds and set of linear polarized feeds covering frequency range of 2 - 40GHz. On the receive side a roll /tower/upper side / Az/El/ Down range side /Cross range side DUT positioner which supports head loads up to 500kg (weight of DUT connected to the roll axis) and 2.4m in diameter. The control room is equipped with RF equipments, control instrumentation allowing fully automated far field measurements, MIDAS far field antenna measurement software, Master computer, analysis workstation. The RF equipment consists of 0.01 to 40GHz Vector network analyzer, RF devices supporting the system operation in the frequency range of 1.0 to 40GHz (expandable to 140GHz) providing minimum dynamic range of 80dB. title: New Facilities at ECIL | ECIL | DAE | India
content: ECIL focuses on providing innovative technology solutions, diversifying product range and developing indigenous solutions to meet customer requirements and the strategic needs of the Nation. Company's R & D strives for development of new products built with cutting-edge technology. Research & Development plus Innovation continues to remain the guiding principles of the company. The Company collaborates with leading R & D organisations, Start-ups and Academic Institutions to develop new technologies and prodcuts. Towards this end, the following new products and technologies were introduced during the current year: Integrated Test Facility for ARMS Upper-Level and Lower-Level Systems serves as platform for conducting interface and integration testing between the Russian-supplied ARMS upper-level system and ECIL-manufactured lower-level ARMS systems. Horizontal Calibration Facility (HCF) for BARCIS for NPCIL has been setup for calibration of Ultrasonic and Eddy Current Probes and check its healthiness. These probes are required for under water head used for inspection of Pressure Tube and measuring the parameters. ECIL has successfully completed the setting up of Advanced Rear End Development (ARED) facility and under XII Five Year Plan. These facilities enable the company to take up in-house production of complex and critical jobs. The test facilities also enables MSMEs to economically utilize these facilities in their product development and delivery. These state of art manufacturing facilitates were inaugurated by Chairman, Atomic Energy Commission & Secretary, Department of Atomic Energy on 31st October, 2021 in the presence of Director, Bhabha Atomic Research Centre. These facilities will further enhance indigenous development & manufacturing of Strategic Products. The X-Band Radio Frequency (RF) Seeker for missile system has been indigenously developed in collaboration with BARC and DRDO. The Seeker is the key contributor to the increased effectiveness of precision strike missile. Post several captive flights and missile flight trials, the missile with indigenous Seeker was successfully test fired and has been cleared for production. Requisite test facility to undertake upto sub system level testing has been setup. Facility for development, testing and qualification of Radiation detectors and Nuclear instruments. This includes Uranium Plating Facility, BF3 Gas Generation & Purification Facility, Charcoal Coating Facility, Helium Leak detection System, Vacuum degradation System, Thermal Cycling Facility for Detectors, Scintillation Crystal growth Facility, Silicon Photo Multiplier & Scintillator Characterisation Facility. These facilities enable in-depth testing and advancement in the field of radiation detection technology. Facility for manufacturing, testing and calibration of X-Ray Generator which is approved by AERB has been setup. Production license for manufacturing of X-Ray Generator and Baggage Inspection System has also been obtained. Cyber Forensics Laboratory has been setup at ECIL towards providing forensic examination to meet requirements of DAE/ Government Organisations. The lab is equipped with latest forensic tools and applications towards secure analysis, recovery and investigation of data. Facility towards design, development, production, testing and repair of Solid State RF Power Amplifiers to meet the requirement of the proposed superconducting accelerator program of DAE / International Mega Science program. This facility is used for the growth and fabrication of Cesium Iodide (CsI) and Sodium Iodide (NaI) crystals, which are used in the production of radiation detectors for various applications related to radiation detection and measurement. It enables the indigenous production of these specific radiation detectors, replacing foreign equivalents. The entire process, from growth to crystal processing, is supported by air shower systems, cleaning and dehydration units, powder loading, and crystal processing facilities.
