title: Make in India (MII) Initiatives | ECIL | DAE | India
content: ECIL has spearheaded the development of Indigenous electronics in the country right from inception and will strive to achieve its cherished goals of 'Atmanirbhar Bharat' by strongly supporting & implementing Govt's initiative on 'Make In India' there by giving further boost to the Indian Industry. The Government’s emphasis on ‘Atmanirbhar Bharat” has given an impetus to the domestic industry to engage, develop and participate in the various sectors and especially with the Government sectors. Several initiatives have been taken by the Government for creating an eco-system for development of technologies through innovation by MSMEs and start-ups. A policy incorporating focus on self-reliance, wherein indigenization and innovation is enabled through processes of make, design & development and strategic partnership, has been promulgated aiming to progressively build indigenous capabilities in the private sector. This is expected to provide a boost to the industry in terms of value and quality products. The substitution for import has been facilitated to reduce lifecycle costs and build a robust ecosystem with the help of the domestic industry /MSMEs. With the changing business scenarios and specific focus on indigenization, ECIL is engaging in building long-term relationships with emerging Strategic Partners both from the Public Sectors, Private Industry, Startups and also Academia for Technology development. Engaging actively with our customers/ users and other key stakeholders in the Defence, Aerospace, Nuclear and Security industry to understand their needs and providing them with the latest in the technology is another of the focus areas towards enhancing business opportunity. ECIL has been supplying Control and Instrumentation Systems, Radiation Detectors and Instruments, Programmable Logical Controllers (PLC), Remote terminal Units(RTU), SCADA systems, Operator Training Simulators of Nuclear Power Plants and Facilities etc., Today, all the nuclear power plants across the country have their vital instrumentation and control systems engineered and manufactured by ECIL indigenously. The government's plan to implement 'Nuclear Energy Mission' for expansion of nuclear power generation in the country, has paved the way for ECIL to actively contribute to Make In India (MII) Program. ECIL has indigenously developed and supplied Secure and Jam-resistant Communications, Electronic Warfare Systems, Simulators, COMINT & Interception Systems, Antenna, SATCOM Systems & Networks, Stabilized platforms for air-borne Radars, C4I & Missile Support Systems, Encryption and Secrecy Systems, Electronic Fuzes, Precision Electro-Mechanical Components, Sensors and Inertial Navigation Systems etc., The Corporation has already developed and supplied many systems/ equipment which are being presently integrated and tested by several DRDO Labs, under the Development cum Production Partner (DcPP) model/initiative of MoD. The aim of this model is to progressively build indigenous capabilities to design, develop and manufacture complex weapon systems and platforms, focusing on self-reliance. ECIL has an expertise in ground segment of Satellite Communication and has been a key player in the major launches of the space satellites. Various types of antennas for Space Programmes, Tri-band Antenna, Satellite Communication Networks for Strategic usage, various gyros and Sensor Instrumentation Package are being indigenously built and supplied by ECIL. The Company is also playing a vital part in the manufacturing of Launch Vehicles and small & micro satellites, for the Indian industry as part of the ISRO's vision. ECIL has also recently established Carbon Fibre Reinforced Polymer (CFRP) facility towards enhanced exploitation and realization of new products. ECIL is providing the legacy security solutions with X-Ray Baggage Inspection System, Integrated Security & Surveillance Systems, Vehicle Mounted Jammers and Classroom Jammers, Access Control Systems and Radiation Detection Equipment (RDEs) to various vital and strategic installations/establishments as part of Make In India Initiatives. The facility towards Chemical, Biological, Radiological & Nuclear (CBRN) threat detection and providing CBRN solutions has been set up and projects in this new field are already being executed by ECIL. ECIL over the years has successfully developed and manufactured EVMs and Voter Verifiable Paper Audit Trail (VVPAT) for Election Commission of India. Technical partnerships towards providing IT and Cyber security solutions have been undertaken as part of Make In India initiatives. The process of mass manufacturing of electronic systems is being implemented by undertaking assembly through contract manufacturing with the state of art facility available in ECIL will give boost to the Make In India Programme. For the Chandrayaan mission, ECIL supplied the 32-meter-deep space network(DSN) antenna, which provides vital communication support. The 300-tonne antenna system was built indigenously in association with Bhabha Atomic Research Centre (BARC), UR Rao Satellite Centre (URSC) and ISTRAC. ECIL has been closely working with ISRO for the indigenous design and realisation of the antennae systems and safe and secure programme logic controllers (PLC) for Mangalyaan-2 mission, as it did for the Chandrayaan-2 and Aditya L1 mission. The indigenous 18-meter antenna, set up by ECIL at Bylalu village about 40 km from Bengaluru, plays a significant role in the communication of ISRO's first observatory-class space-based solar mission from India - Aditya L1. ECIL vehicle-mounted jammers helped secure G20 perimeter against any threat emanating during the just-concluded G20 summit in New Delhi attended by prominent world leaders. ECIL has been providing increased thrust towards the procurement from MSMEs and further impetus since the introduction of Public Procurement Policy for MSEs. The procurement of products and services from Micro and Small Enterprises during the last financial year achieved is 25%. ECIL has been consistently putting efforts to achieve 4% procurement from SC/ST & 3% procurement from Women entrepreneurs. More entrepreneurs from SC, ST & Women category are been encouraged to register with ECIL through special Vendor Development program been conducted at regular intervals. LIST OF ITEMS RESERVED FOR PURCHASE FROM MICRO AND SMALL ENTERPRISES (Incl. List of Items Reserved for Purchase from Handicrafts Sector) as per Government Guidelines. ** (pdf /26.18 KiB ) ** The Document is sourced from the Portal of Development Commissioner, Ministry of MSME, GoI. To facilitate the same, ECIL has well established procedures to carry out purchase, sub-contract and works contract activities as per the respective manuals approved by the Competent Authority. title: Sustainable Development (SD) Initiatives | ECIL | DAE | India
content: ECIL believes in conducting its business activities in a responsible and sustainable manner and is actively pursuing toward good Environmental, Social and Governance perspectives. ECIL is working towards transparent environment and is responsive to all its stakeholders. ECIL as a CPSE is also publishing the Sustainable development efforts in a "Stand Alone Report" or as a separate charter in the Annual Report inline with the DPE Guidelines. ECIL has identified the following as major thrust areas towards sustainable development efforts. Thrust areas for sustainable development are: Two Effluent Treatment plants (ETPs) were constructed one with a capacity of 300 kl/day and second one with a capacity of 650 kl/day to treat the effluent generated from process. Apart from the above, recycling of effluent generated from process, domestic sewerage and silage in the existing ETPs is also being done. Regular maintenance of ETP plants is being carried for reduction and control of Effluent. Replacement of faulty / outlived valves, motors and other plumbing fittings & fixtures undertaken in a time bound manner to avoid wastage and conserve water. Treated water from ETP is being used for gardening / horticulture purposes in lieu of fresh water. HDPE pipelines have been laid to supply the treated water. Messages are displayed at appropriate places to sensitise the employees to save water by reducing the wastage of water since water saved is water conserved. Above efforts have resulted in reducing the fresh water consumption of about 300 kilo Litres per Day. Thereby maintaining the aquatic environment and reducing the fresh water requirement of same amount which can be utilized for other applications. Apart from the above, Rain Water Harvesting Pits with injection Bore Wells are operational which resulted in increase in ground water level and quality of the ground water. Towards energy conservation measures ECIL setup 500KWp Ground Mounted Grid Interactive Solar Power plant and synchronized with grid. With this the total Solar Power plant capacity in ECIL is increased to 1050KWp. This initiative is to use alternate source of energy. The Solar Power Plant generated 8,93,217 KWH units during the FY 2024-25. As part of Waste Management efforts, separate bins for different categories of wastage have been constructed in the factory premises. Collection of e-waste and segregation of e-waste from all other wastes is also being undertaken. 1100 MT. of Municipal solid waste (MSW) was disposed to Hyderabad Integrated Waste Management Facility managed by M/s Ramky Enviro Engineers Private Limited. With the disposal, public health is maintained and protected from various contaminations. ECIL has taken steps for Collection and Storage of e-Waste under Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR). Accordingly, End of life e-Waste of Electronic equipment manufactured by ECIL like Electronic Voting Machines are collected, transported and disposed ensuring no damage to the environment during storage and transportation. As part of Company’s initiative to increase the green cover in the factory premises, plants / saplings of various types including fruit bearing were planted across the Corporation on various inaugural/ceremonial events/VIP Visits and other occasions. The existing vermi compost plant produced Fifteen Hundred kilogram of manure. The manure generated is being used for in-house gardening and nursery development. The above initiative resulted in reducing the soil erosion, improving air quality and maintaining the ecological balance in the Factory premises. As part of Environmental Monitoring initiatives, various testes are carried out every month to analyse the effluent from ETP’s, noise level and monitoring of Air Quality. Display of wall posters on environmental protection is undertaken to sensitise employees and visitors. With the above-mentioned Environmental & Sustainability initiatives, ECIL was able to leverage its resources to nurture the Natural Capital for future generations. Water Conservation; Energy Conservation; Waste Management & E-Waste Disposal; Green Cover & Environmental Monitoring
summary: ECIL believes in conducting its business activities in a responsible and sustainable manner and is actively pursuing toward good Environmental, Social and Governance perspectives. content: Right from inception, ECIL has been a Technology-driven Company. Starting with supporting the Country's Atomic Energy Programme, the Company pioneered a number of technologies and introduced a number of products for the first time in the Country. ECIL strongly believes that human capital with right experience and skill set plays a crucial role in the growth of the organisation. With this philosophy, the Company continued its best efforts in recruiting the people with right skill and experience and continued to prioritize their development and well-being. Our HR initiatives focus on Training and Development, Employee Facilities & Welfare and Optimal Utilization of manpower by initiating number of programmes to retrain and redeploy the existing manpower so as to ensure gainful employment and achievement of targets. ECIL was setup under the DAE with a view to generating a strong indigenous capability in the field of professional grade electronics. The company, which started as a manufacturing company wedded to indigenisation and self-reliance had a majority of human resources deployed in manufacturing operations. The post-liberalization era posed a number of challenges to the company especially in the area of HR, Due to the right sizing and restructuring compelled by the market forces. The Company continued its best efforts in recruiting the people with right skill and experience and currently engaging the manpower in the following categories. The global village creators aftermath of liberalization, privatization and globalization attracted many well trained technologists and managers from the Company and as a result the reservoir of the competencies started depleting. Attrition has become global phenomena and the worst hit is the Electronics & IT field. Customer requirements are also changing dynamically and many of them, especially in the areas of Strategic Electronics, are expecting Total solutions. In a highly competitive market environment, with outsourcing as a business inevitability, every operation needs to hire the services of Experts in select areas. Today, atleast a multi-disciplinary organization like ECIL, it is very difficult, if not impossible to have the required expertise within the organization. The age of the organization and also the retirement profile also aggravates the situation. Therefore, top management of the Company decided to hire the services of experts in the areas of relevance to the Company, to supplement the efforts of the Project Teams in the Strategic Business Units and other service functions. The required expertise is sought in those areas, which are depleted due to superannuation and some specialized areas which are non-existent to required levels within Company and also essential. As a Policy, ECIL appoints experts in the following levels as "Senior Technical Experts" (OR) "Technical Experts". ECIL has focused on training & development of its human resource so as to build highly motivated teams to achieve its objectives. Accordingly, ECIL has established a system for continuous assessment of training requirements of its employees and organised various Internal/ External Training Programs in the broad categories of Technical, Functional / Certification and Behavioural aspects towards enhancing the skill set/knowledge of its work force over the years. Training was imparted by faculty invited from reputed institutions as well as internal faculty and has resulted in more than 1000 plus man-days of Training per year in Offline/Class Room Mode. The work force has significant number of Women employees who are shouldering the responsibilities at various positions including the senior management level. In order to ensure the availability of quality and enhanced health care coverage to employees and their dependent family members, ECIL has introduced Group Mediclaim Medical Insurance Scheme which is a cashless medical treatment facility in the network hospitals of the insurance provider across the country with maximum insurance coverage. The provisions contained in the Maternity Benefit Act are strictly followed and the female employees (incl. Regular on-roll employees & FTE’s) were provided with Maternity leaves (including for Miscarriages). Paternity Leave was also extended in compliance with the Government of India Guidelines. In addition to above, reimbursement of expenditure incurred towards In-Vitro Fertilization (IVF) treatment to employees with a capping per employee is introduced in compliance with the Government of India Guidelines. ECIL believes that prevention is better than cure. Towards this philosophy as well as complying with the applicable regulations, preventive health check-ups were conducted for employees who are on Regular rolls as well as on contract and contract labour working in hazardous areas working at different sites and Head Quarters. Medical Examinations were also conducted for Senior Executives. Towards enhancing the availability of quality health care at affordable cost to its employees and their dependent family members, ECIL has empanelled various Government, Private Hospitals and Diagnostic Centres for providing treatment on credit basis & non-credit basis. Apart from the above, ECIL has facilitated the medical treatment at CGHS Tariffs for contract manpower deployed by the contractors in ECIL at par with its regular employees through empanelled hospitals. The dispensary facility established in the DAE Colony/ township was augmented and is available on all working days of ECIL. Crèche facility was also extended to the children of contract manpower. A well-defined policy is in place in ECIL for redressal of grievances of the employees. In line with the Government of India initiatives in promoting holistic wellbeing and environmental harmony of employees, International Yoga Day is being celebrated on 21st June of each year at Head Quarters and at Zonal Offices wherein employees at all levels are participating in large numbers with zeal and enthusiasm. To ensure safety & health of ECIL workforce, training was imparted on Industrial Safety and Occupational Health to the employees in addition to the mock drills. Medical examinations were carried out for the employees working in hazardous areas. To enhance regular compliance to various statutory requirements quarterly internal audits were carried out in all the production areas by safety team within the organization. To promote safety culture and to make employees participate in safety activities, various competitions are being conducted during National Safety Day and Fire Services Week. ECIL has conducted Third Party surveillance audit and is certified with the Occupational Health and Safety Certification (ISO 45001:2018) and Environmental Management Systems Certification (ISO 14001:2015). In addition, to achieve Optimum levels of Occupational, Health & Safety and Environmental performance, Online Safety Work Permit System and Online Near-miss Incident Reporting Systems were introduced. In line with the requirement under the provisions of Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013, and Rules made there under, Internal Complaints Committee (ICC) is in place to redress the complaints regarding sexual harassment. The ICC meets on regular basis to review the status and Employees are made aware about PoSH related guidelines from time to time through Posters and Workshops. All employees (permanent, contractual, temporary, trainees) are covered under this policy. All Divyangjan employees, be it Extraneous Manpower, Regular or Apprentices are being provided the facilities as per the laid down guidelines from time to time. Divyangjans are provided with allowances and other exemptions during the recruitment. All Safety requirements of Divyangjan employees at workplaces is taken care of by allowing their personal vehicles inside the factory premises and allowing them to move freely in the compound. They are being provided with additional privileges like grace time during entry/exit to enable hassle free movement at the gates. All necessary provisions are made for their special needs at the work places and toilets. It may be noted that the Company has complied with the Government of India guidelines on reservations. content: ECIL is providing excellent facilities to employees and their dependents and the details are mentioned below: DAE Colony is one of the residential Township of the Department of Atomic Energy. It is the residential complex consisting of about 1500 flats for the employees of various units of Department of Atomic Energy of the Government of India in ECIL, Hyderabad area. It has residential flats, local grocery shops, sports and recreation facilities, schools, medical clinics, post office and transport links to many parts of the city. The complex is sprawling and lies stretched out with the abundant green natural environment. Hills, lakes, flowers, Trees, etc. add more natural feeling to the campus. In order to ensure the availability of quality and enhanced health care coverage to employees and their dependent family members, ECIL has introduced Group Mediclaim Medical Insurance Scheme which is a cashless medical treatment facility in the network hospitals of the insurance provider across the country with maximum insurance coverage. Towards enhancing the availability of quality health care at affordable cost to its employees and their dependent family members, ECIL has empanelled various Government, Private Hospitals and Diagnostic Centres for providing treatment on credit basis & non-credit basis. Apart from the above, ECIL has facilitated the medical treatment at CGHS Tariffs for contract manpower deployed by the contractors in ECIL at par with its regular employees through empanelled hospitals. The Atomic Energy Education Society (AEES) provides education facility up to Intermediate level to the children of employees who reside in and around DAE Colony. The children of ECIL employees are given preference for admission. Atomic Energy Central School is governed by AEES(Atomic Energy Education Society-Mumbai) a Governing Council consisting of members of the Department of Atomic Energy. A Baby Creche is organised in the Company for the benefit of female employees to keep their children up to the age of 6 years. Free milk and biscuits are provided to the children. The trained staff would take care of the children during their stay in the Creche and mothers are allowed to visit their children as per the stipulated timings. The Baby Creche is a unique day care centre for 30 children consisting of infants, toddler and school going upto 6 years of age. It takes to spacious playful outdoors, colourful charming indoors and above all blessed by Mother Nature. Here the children keep meeting Sea and Sky and books and toys again and again. It aims at providing quality care based on modern, scientific and professional principles to children of the families where both parents are working. The objective is to make the Day Care Center a home away from home. The Baby Creche aims to provide a safe, secure and stimulating place for the children. The Crèche facility has been extended to the children of contract manpower also in recent times. The transport facilities are provided to the employees for commuting from their place of residence to factory and back possibly at zero-subsidized rates, by hiring the TSRTC buses. There are presently 9 buses being operated for the said purposes shuttling between length and breadth of the twin cities and adjoining Ranga Reddy District. One of the prime functions of Transport Section is to run the buses at the lowest possible costs, through shortest possible routes. The Transport Committee comprising both members of Management, OA and Union undertakes surveys and recommend re- routing of Buses to ensure economy in operations. The charges levied are also revised to achieve zero-subsidy level. Adequate canteen/lunch room facilities are provided as required under the provisions of Factories Act and AERB Regulations. At present ECIL has one CENTRAL Canteen with sub-canteens. A Canteen Managing Committee is formed with Head(HR) as the Chairman and equal representation of both workmen and management. The food-items supplied in the canteen are highly subsidized. The canteen food rates will be worked out once in a year and after considering the cost incurred/services provided in cash or kind and would be charged at such rates. Lunch Rooms are also provided outside the Factory entrance gate/Administration Building to enable the employees to have lunch brought by them during lunch hour. A well furnished Guesthouse is situated outside but very close to the factory premises. It provides accommodation to outstation employees/guests of Divisions on official duties. It provides comfortable accommodation (VIP Rooms, AC Rooms) and dining facilities (VIP Dining and General Dining) to bona fide guests. There are 4 VVIP & 4 VIP Suits, 17 AC Rooms and 2 Non AC rooms. AC and Non AC rooms are provided with 2 single beds, cable TV and attached bathrooms. The rooms are allotted against the requisitions received from Divisions through HOD/Branch In-charges, mentioning their arrival and departure details and whether the Division or the guest will make the payments (including breakfast/dinner). Divisions should send their guest/guests accommodation requirements one week in advance and contact the Guesthouse to confirm their booking at least 48 hrs. in advance. For Trainees, like Graduate Engineer Trainees, the quarters will be allotted on sharing basis, i.e. One quarter for two or three trainees depends upon availability of quarters at that time. The allotment will be made on first-cum-first basis for the employees for a particular type of quarter and in the event of competition from more than one employee for allotment of a particular quarter, the seniormost employee will be allotted the said quarter. DAE colony people together celebrates almost all the festivals that are celebrated across the country such as, Holi, Diwali, Durga Puja, Dussehra, Onam, Gudi padwa, Pongal, Ganesh Utsav, Dhai Handi, Id, Christmas Day, Independence day, Republic day and the list goes on. Here we can see unity in diversity, a peculiar feature of our nation. These festivals bring wonderful enthusiasm and energy among each other, which creates a friendly bonding, a unity in team spirit and great opportunity in network building as well as socio-cultural interaction and harmony among the culturally diverse people. The Estate Management and Maintenance, Nuclear Fuel Complex will look after proper maintenance repairs and alterations of the quarters. The employee shall take possession of the residence allotted from the authorities of Estate Management and shall also at the time of vacating the quarters handing over the same to the said authority. A First-Aid Medical Centre/Dispensary is provided inside the factory to meet the emergencies. This Centre is provided with the facility of five beds (two for Male employees, two for Female employees and one at EMSD) which is used in cases which require observation under medical care, for certain duration of time. The same is under the control of CMO, First Aid Centre and supported by other Medical Officers and with nursing staff. The cases of sudden development of sickness/accidents of employees at work place are referred to First-Aid Centre, for immediate medical attention/evaluation. Based on the condition of the patient and diagnosis, he/she is referred to a Specialist/Hospital on panel. In this First-Aid Centre/Dispensary the employees who come as patients are medically examined and provided with medicines wherever required. The medicines that are made available in this Centre are generally of first-aid nature and some lifesaving drugs/injections. Ambulance service is available round the clock, at the disposal of CMO, First Aid Centre during working hours and later on under the control of Duty Officer of CISF at Main Gate. The dispensary facility established in the DAE Colony/ township was augmented and is available on all working days of ECIL. Further, a Dispensary is also operational in the DAE Housing Colony for the benefit of employees/family members who are residing in the Colony during every Monday Afternoon and one of the Medical Officer along with nursing staff takes care of same. ECIL believes that prevention is better than cure. Towards this philosophy as well as complying with the applicable regulations, preventive health check-ups were conducted for employees who are on Regular rolls as well as on contract and contract labour working in hazardous areas working at different sites and Head Quarters. Medical Examinations were also conducted for Senior Executives. At present AECS mans the Schools at Anushakthi Nagar and Tarapur(Maharashtra), Hyderabad and Manuguru(Andhra pradesh), Narora(Uttarpradesh), Kakrapar(Gujarat), Oscam(Orissa), Indore(Madhya Pradhesh), Rawathbhata(Rajasthan), Anupuram, Kalpakkam and Kudangulam(Tamilnadu), Kaiga and Mysore(Karnataka), Jaduguda and Narwapahar(Jharkhand). The first school by the AECS was begun in the year 1969, in Anushaktinagar,Mumbai, to cater to the needs of educating children / wards of employees of the Dept. of Atomic Energy. The AEES has added schools commensurate with the growth of the activities in DAE and consequent increase in the strength of employees. Today, in Hyderabad, there are 2 schools and one junior college with a total student strength of about 3000. To address the needs of these students 200 staff members work in the schools. Each school is complete with the requisite number of teachers & staff, infrastructure, laboratories & grounds for sports and games. The School runs classes from pre-prep to tenth class. Atomic energy education society (AEES) endeavours to empower its students with wide spectrum of knowledge to prepare them to become responsible citizens of the country. Furthermore, AEES is determined to inculcate in its students. Attitude and expertise required for the worldliness, patriotism, exemplary moral values and respect towards the rich culture of the nation. We also encourage our students for eradication of differences based on caste, creed, gender, religion and language.

title: Employee Trainings | ECIL | DAE | India
content: ECIL values human resources as the most important asset. All the available human resources are facilitated to acquire, update and share their knowledge and skills in order to achieve the vision, mission and objectives of the corporation. ECIL, since its inception, through design and development, has been innovative in various India's key and critical sectors such as defence, Railways, shipyards, aerospace, nuclear power plants, banking, health and internal security, complex electronic components/instruments etc. Therefore, keeping in view of the constant emerging/changing technical advancements, more emphasis is given on the need for continuous and rapid updating of skills. To achieve both long and short term goals and objectives, ECIL pays maximum attention on various management as well as technological update training programmes with respect to various business Areas/Groups/Divisions. This responsibility is vested on Corporate Learning & Development Center (CLDC) situated in the lush green environment which is actively engaged in organizing required trainings from external/internal expert agency/faculty. Through the group training co-ordinators, CLDC is actively engaged in identification of personnel to be trained along with suitable training programs and maintains necessary records for the same. All the new hires are provided with the 'Induction-cum-Orientation Program' which includes the organization's product profile, rules and regulations etc. An exclusive visit to all the units of the Factory is also conducted as part of this training programme. Before the commencement of each financial year, CLDC meets the functional directors/Executive Directors/General Managers, departmental heads and interim managers to take their advice and conducts an innovative study to assess the training and developmental needs across the corporation. As part of its responsibility, special emphasis is given on the skill gaps related to various ongoing and future business needs both at division level and corporate level and these gaps can be bridged through collaboration with other organizations engaged in engineering and technological sectors. Based on this analysis, comprehensive Annual Training Plan is prepared and after taking necessary approvals, organizes lectures/seminars/workshops either in-house or external both in India and abroad based on the training and resource requirements. It is also responsible to collect both formal and informal feedback from the participants regarding the training programmes conducted for further improvements. When an employee participates specifically in an external training program, he is required to share the training details with his colleagues and subordinates in a session which is headed by the Head of the Division he belongs to. All the training material has to be handed over to CLDC and to be hosted in the intranet for accessibility to all employees. Incharge - CLDC Corporate Learning & Development Centre (CLDC) Nalanda Complex, ECIL, ECIL Post, Hyderabad -500062.

title: Apprenticeship Opportunities for Candidates | ECIL | DAE | India
content: ECIL, a Public Sector Enterprise under the Department of Atomic Energy is engaging the various apprentices at ECIL Hyderabad under the Apprenticeship Act 1961. CLDC is actively coordinating with various government authorities and looks after the overall apprenticeship activities and maintains necessary records for the same. As per the ECIL Trainee Regulations, Trainees are appointed in the following categories: All the above categories of trainees are appointed as per the quota applicable in the rules and regulations of the education board authorities. The graduate holders of Electronics and Communication Engineering, Computer Science and Engineering, Information Technology, Electrical and Electronics Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Civil Engineering etc., are appointed for a maximum period of one year in the units corresponding to their respective disciplines. Diploma holders are appointed for a period of one year/six months which depends on whether they are eligible for Technician Apprenticeship scheme or not. Graduate Engineer Apprentices and Technician Apprentices both are monitored and regulated by the Board of Apprenticeship Training (BOA), Chennai, Ministry of Education, Government of India. The students having NCTVT Certificate approved by Industrial Training Institute in various trades like Electronics, Mechanics, Fitter, Electrical, Welding, Air-condition mechanics, Carpentry, Automobile Mechanics, Turners, Millers, Sheet etc. are appointed as trade apprentices as per trade-wise quota. The only agency regulating this type of training is the Directorate of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (RDSDE), Hyderabad and the scheme is funded by the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE)which is under the Government of India. The Shop Floor training duration depends on the total duration of the training. All the categories of apprentice are selected by CLDC. Applications are invited from candidates of various trades. The candidates have to produce SSC, Trade Certificate and Marks Memo for verification. The eligible candidates are shortlisted on the basis of merit and approved accordingly. The CLDC communicates the same to the candidates and starts the training programme. Every apprentice is required to sign a contract as per the apprenticeship rules and regulations that includes the rules regarding leaves etc. The signed contract agreements are sent to the ITI Board, Chennai for registration upon which the apprentice is assigned a Registration number. Service including holiday allowance etc. as per contract. The training includes details regarding their roles, responsibilities and code of conduct and posted to different units where their progress of work is monitored on a regular basis. On completion of the training period, Trade apprentices have to undergo All India Trade Examination and the apprentices who are successful in this examination will be certified by MSDE. On successful completion of the prescribed period of training, apprenticeship certificates are also issued to graduate and vocational apprentices. In respect of Graduate and Technician apprentices, 50% of the stipend is reimbursed by ITI Board, Chennai upon prescribed claims for the duration of the training period. In case of ITI Apprentice, MSDE reimburses 25% of the scholarship upto a maximum amount of Rs.1500 per month. The Payroll section of Finance & Accounts Group co-ordinates with CLDC in settling the claims. content: Complaints, if any, complainant can lodge online complaints using Lodge Complaint (or) write an email to CVO, ECIL at cvo@ecil.co.in (or) can drop complaints in the "Complaint Box" located at Office of CVO, ECIL (or) can send complaints through post addressed to CVO, ECIL. Complainants/whistle blowers are requested to provide their identity (Name, Address and Contact details) as verification of authenticity of complaint and it is mandatory prior to investigation by Vigilance Department as per CVC guidelines. Complainants/Whistle Blowers, who desires to keep their identity confidential may lodge complaint using PIDPI resolution as per CVC act (info placed under the tab “Protection of Informer” ) or as per Whistle Blower Policy of ECIL ( info placed under the tab “ Whistle Blower Policy” ). The Central Vigilance Commission acts as an apex organization for exercising general superintendence and control over vigilance matters in administration and probity in public life. The CVC provides necessary guidelines for effectively carrying out vigilance administration in Government of India departments through various circulars/directives. These circulars/directives can be downloaded from the CVC Website. Vigilance Administration in ECIL, a PSU under Department of Atomic Energy, Government of India, is headed by a Chief Vigilance Officer. The CVO acts as an Advisor to the Chairman and Managing Director, ECIL, in all matters pertaining to Vigilance. CVO acts as a link between the PSU, the Ministry and the CBI. Vigilance functions that are carried out by the office of the CVO include collecting intelligence about the corrupt practices committed, or likely to be committed by the employees of the organization, investigating or causing an investigation to be made into verifiable allegations reported to him/her; processing investigation reports for consideration of the Disciplinary Authorities; referring the matter to the Central Vigilance Commission wherever necessary; taking steps to prevent commissioning improper practices/misconduct etc. Thus, the functions of the office of CVO can broadly be divided into the following three parts: (iii) surveillance and detection. While surveillance and punitive action are for commission of misconduct and other malpractices, the preventive measures taken by the CVO are considered more important as these are meant to reduce the number of vigilance cases considerably. Central Vigilance Commission (CVC) issued Standard Operating Procedure for implementation of Integrity Pact (IP) requirement which is aimed at preventing corruption and ensuring integrity in public procurements. Integrity Pact shall be applicable for procurements of a value exceeding Rs. 2 Crore and above. content: The Company has put in place an appropriate mechanism for promoting transparency and accountability in compliance to the requirements under Right to Information Act, 2005. The Company has nominated Central Public Information Officer/First Appellate Authority at its Corporate Office and DPIOs at the Divisional level to provide the required information under the provisions of the Act. In line with the Government directives, the company is processing online applications as per provisions under the RTI Act. The FAA, CPIO and other internal stakeholders involved in the process are nominated for training and workshops to get more acquaintance with the requirements and obligations under the Act. Quarterly returns for all the quarters of the year are being submitted to Central Information Commission. Third party Audit of proactive disclosure package was completed in accordance with the OM Dt. 07.11.2019 issued by Department of Personnel and Training, Government of India. Particulars of Organization i.e. ECIL are indicated in the About Us , Business Verticals , Human Resources sections of the website. ECIL is a MOU signing Company with Department of Atomic Energy (DAE), Govt. of India (GoI). The details of Revenue from Operations, authorised share capital and the Dividend details etc., are mentioned in the Annual Reports hosted under the Financials section. To know more about the Company financials Click here The Company has organized its business operations Division-wise under SBU concept, bringing products of related technologies under one Division each. Addresses of ECIL Registered Office, Factories and Zonal / Branch Offices: ECIL is a commercial organization with well defined powers and duties. Important powers and duties are given below: As Chief Executive, he is accountable to its Board of Directors. He is responsible for optimization of resources and achieving Company objectives. He has the powers to - Director(Personnel) is a member of the Board of Directors. He reports to Chairman & Managing Director. He is overall in-charge of coordinating and implementing personnel and industrial relations policies. He has the powers to - Director(Finance) is a member of Board of Directors. He reports to Chairman and Managing Director. He is overall In-charge of Finance and Accounts. He is responsible for evolving and formulating finance policies as well as implementation thereof. He has the power to - Director (Technical) is a member of Board of Directors. He reports to Chairman and Managing Director. He is overall in-charge of technical functions covering R&D, production and marketing. He is responsible for optimum utilization of resources. He advises on safety matters. He has the power to - The General Managers are responsible for the operations of the Divisions under their administrative control. They will organize materials and manpower to achieve the Divisional targets. They have the powers for - The Heads of the Divisions are responsible for the operations of their respective Divisions. They generally report to GM concerned. They have the necessary powers for the production and sales of the Division concerned. Presently, ECIL has three manufacturing facilities (two at Hyderabad and one at Tirupati) and Zonal / Branch Offices, Regional Maintenance Centers (RMCs) / Sub-Regional Maintenance Centers (SRMCs) spread across the Country. The SRMCs are under the administrative control of respective RMCs and the RMCs are under the administrative control of Respective Zonal / Branch Offices. The Zonal Managers are under the administrative control of the Director (Technical). The operations at Head Office are organized into Business Divisions (SBUs) and Services Divisions. The Organization Chart depicting the Organization’s structure is available at Organizaton Setup under the "About Us" section of the ECIL Website. The decisions making process in the Company at higher levels involves the following channels. The Company has notified various procedures, guidelines, schemes and rules to the Employees for discharge of their functions. To meet the changing business needs, the Company issues new rules, modifies the existing rules and notifies them through established internal channels of communication for due compliance by employees. The Organization follows the guidelines issued from time to time by Department of Public Enterprises and Central Vigilance Commission. The important Rules, Regulations, Manuals and Schemes which are notified to the Employees for compliance in discharging their functions, are indicated below: All Statutory Registers/Documents are maintained under Companies Act and other applicable Laws. In addition, following categories of documents are also held by the organization or under its control: The Board of Directors of ECIL covering the Whole Time Functional Directors, Part-Time (Government / Independent) Directors are indicated in the "About Us -> Board of Directors & CVO" section of the website and is updated on a regular basis. Licenses from Technology Suppliers Annual Reports for the years 2006-07 to 2024-25; Current Tenders for purchase of goods/services; Current Advertisements for Jobs; Press Releases Procedure for seeking information and inspection of records under The Right to Information Act, 2005 (hereinafter 'Act') 1.1 Procedure to obtain information from the Central Public Information Officer (CPIO): 1.1.1 The Central Assistant Public Information Officer (CAPIO)/Central Public Information Officer (CPIO) have been designated as mentioned at Chapter- XVI to receive the request seeking information. 1.1.2 Any Indian citizen who desires to obtain any information, or inspection of records, under the provisions of this Act, shall make a request in writing or through electronic means in Form-A or Form-B (given in the following pages), as the case may be to the CAPIO/CPIO. These forms are available with Reception Section at Head Quarters free of cost or the requester can take print of the same from ECIL website www.ecil.co.in by himself or write a letter in the same format. The request shall accompany such fee as prescribed under the Act. 1.1.3 Requester shall not make a request for information or inspection of records which are exempted from disclosure under Sections 8 and 9 of the Act. 1.1.4 Requester shall mention in application whether the information sought for concerns the life or liberty of a person. 1.1.5 The Reply shall be either collected by requester or shall be forwarded to the requester either through post or courier, at the address given in the application form. 1.1.6 Requests which are not addressed to CAPIO/CPIO or not specifying the exact information required shall not be responded. 1.2 Time Schedule CPIO will send the response to requester within the period as specified under the Act. 1.3 Applicable fee and payments: 1.3.1 Each application for seeking information/inspection of records shall be accompanied by an application fee of Rs. 10/- by way of DD/ Bankers Cheque/Indian Postal Order. The Applicant can also pay the Application fee of Rs.10/- by way of cash to the Accounts Officer, Electronics Corporation of India Limited, at Head Quarters, against proper Receipt, during normal working hours, personally or through his representative. 1.3.2 Fee for providing information/inspection of records will be as follows: Rs. 2/- for each page (in A-4 or A-3 size Paper), created or copied Actual charge or cost price of a copy in larger size paper Actual cost or price for samples or models; Rs. 50/- per diskette or floppy containing information; Information in printed form: price fixed for publication or Rs. 2/- per page of photocopy for extracts from the publication. Inspection of records: No fee for first hour; a fee of Rs. 5/- for each subsequent hour ( or fraction thereof) 1.3.3 Request shall be accepted only when it is related to CAPIO/CPIO under the Act and is accompanied by the requisite fee as specified above at 1.3.1 above 1.3.4 In case required, CPIO shall inform the requester about additional fee to be deposited by him towards furnishing of information or inspection of records. The Requester, upon getting notice from CPIO, shall deposit the additional fee requested in connection with the processing of the request, promptly, prior to release of information/inspection of documents. The CPIO shall not be responsible for delays occurred on account of the late receipt of additional payments from the requester. 1.3.5 In case the mode of payment is through Demand Draft or Banker's Cheque/Indian Postal Order, the same shall be issued in favor of Accounts Officer, Electronics Corporation of India Limited or in favour of Electronics Corporation of India Limited. 1.3.6 Application along with the money receipt towards cash payment or the Demand Draft or Banker's Cheque or Indian Postal Order shall be accepted by CAPIO/CPIO. 1.3.7 Requester shall not enclose any currency note(s) along with the application, delivered through post / courier as it is against provisions of the Act and also the rules governing postal services. 1.3.8 Requester shall not deposit fee in excess of what is prescribed. Any extra money deposited with the Public Authority could be claimed by the requester latest within 30 days from date of furnishing of reply by CPIO. In any case, such extra amount shall not be considered against any other request for information. 1.3.9 Requester who is Below Poverty Line(BPL) need not pay any fee. He/she will have to, however, show the ration card applicable to person below poverty line and submit a copy of same along with application. title: Business Enquiry | ECIL | DAE | India
content: ECIL is a multi-product, multi-disciplinary and multi-technology organization providing cutting-edge technology solutions in the strategic areas of Nuclear Power and Process Control, Defence, Aerospace, Homeland Security, IT and e-Governance. We welcome your interest in our Products / Solutions / Services and our Corporate Business Development & Marketing (CBDM) Team will co-ordinate with respective ECIL team members & assist you in fulfilling your business requirements at the earliest possible time. The enquirers are requested to click on the 'Place a Business Enquiry' button to provide your business requirements. A Unique 'Business Enquiry ID' will be generated by the system and an email containing the 'Business Enquiry Details' will be sent to the ECIL team along with a copy to the enquirer. The enquirers are requested to invariably quote the 'Business Enquiry ID' for further correspondence with the ECIL team. The enquirers can check the Latest Status of the Submitted Business Enquiry using the "Status Check" option given below. They can also contact the CBDM team for necessary assistance and support. For enquiries related to Employee Facilities / Trainings, Current Job Openings, Shortlists / Results, Apprenticeship / Project Opportunities and Reference Formats etc., please check the webpages under Human Resources Menu (or) contact the Recruitment Team for further information and support. All fields marked with an asterisk * are mandatory

content: As a Public Enterprise under the Department of Atomic Energy, Quality, Safety and Environmental Management have been the areas of focus ever since inception of the company. This focus has been continuously buttressed by the Quality Assurance Agencies of the customers, regulatory agencies like the Atomic Energy regulatory Board and the Pollution Control Boards. The company developed well laid out strategies and policies for Quality, Safety, Environment and achieved certification as per applicable International Standards. Recently the company has also initiated steps to get Certification for Information Security Management. Quality and Customer Satisfaction are an essential part of the annual MoU signed with the Government of India. As we value feedback from our esteemed customers like you, we request you to kindly send us your feedback online. The customers are requested to submit their feedback by clicking on "Online Customer Feedback" in the submenu bar present in this page. The customers who wish to submit the manually filled-in feedback are requested to click on "Download Customer Feedback Format", fill all the details and upload the filled-in feedback form by clicking on "Upload Feedback Report" in the submenu bar present in this page. Information given by you will be treated as confidential. We look forward for your feedback to improve our quality of services. title: Profile of Dr. Anesh Kumar Sharma, OS, Director (Technical) (Holding Addl. Charge of C&MD) | ECIL | DAE | India
tags: Profile of Dr. Anesh Kumar Sharma, OS, Director (Technical) (Holding Addl. Charge of C&MD)
content: Dr. Anesh Kumar Sharma, OS Director (Technical) Holding Addl. Charge of Chairman & Managing Director Dr. Anesh Kumar Sharma assumed charge as Director (Technical) on the Board of Electronics Corporation of India Limited (ECIL) , a Government of India Enterprise under the Department of Atomic Energy (DAE) , on 27th May 2022 . An Outstanding Scientist with the Defence Research & Development Organisation (DRDO) , Dr. Sharma brings with him over three decades of distinguished experience spanning semiconductors, defence systems, aerospace, secure communication, RF & Microwave systems, and mission-critical electronics . Adjunct Professor at IIT Gandhinagar , actively mentoring the next generation of technologists and strengthening industry - academia collaboration. Dr. Sharma’s professional journey began at Semi-Conductor Complex Ltd. (SCL), Chandigarh , where he worked in semiconductor technologies and contributed to the development of Monolithic Microwave Integrated Circuits (MMICs) at GAETEC - a joint initiative of SCL and DRDO. Before joining ECIL, Dr. Sharma served as Project Director, Naval Anti-Ship Missile - Short Range (NASM - SR) at Research Centre Imarat (RCI), DRDO , Hyderabad, successfully leading developmental trials at ITR Chandipur in collaboration with the Indian Navy. Prior to this, he was Associate Project Director of MRSAM (IAF) - a joint DRDO - IAI Israel program - where he played a pivotal role in developing indigenous missile-associated electronics, RF seekers, MMICs and mission-critical subsystems . MRSAM system has been inducted in IAF and it is in Service. He has also been associated, directly and indirectly, with NASM-SR, MRSAM, BrahMos and Aakash programs , contributing significantly to India’s self-reliance in defence electronics . His international exposure includes heading Design and Acceptance Reviews with IAI Israel for MRSAM and NASM-SR programs. As Director (Technical), Dr. Sharma leads ECIL’s strategic verticals: Nuclear Systems, Defence Electronics, Aerospace, Homeland Security, and IT & e-Governance . His portfolio includes oversight of R&D, production, business growth and futuristic technology initiatives across the organization. One of his most critical national responsibilities is steering the production, quality and timely deployment of Electronic Voting Machines (EVMs) for the world’s largest democratic exercise - a contribution of global significance. He has guided ECIL towards indigenous innovation, startup collaboration, industry - academia tie-ups, and cutting-edge technology development . Under the leadership, ECIL has diversified into new technology domains for futuristic product requirements. Under his leadership, ECIL has recently secured several patents in areas like optical sensing, prismatic lenses, battery life estimation, access detection, and laser-based reflective sensing systems . Dr. Sharma’s contributions have been recognized with numerous prestigious awards at national and institutional levels, including: Under his current tenure, ECIL has also been conferred with several national recognitions such as: Ph.D. in Micro Electronics Engineering - IIT Hyderabad; M.E. in Electronics & Communication Engineering - Osmania University; B.E. in Electronics & Power Engineering; MBA - Blending technical expertise and managerial acumen ELCINA Special Jury award for the Outstanding Contribution to development of Strategic Electronics and Critical infrastructure for the year 2024-25 (2025); Alumni Award for Distinguished Contributions towards Society and Nation Building by IIT Hyderabad (2022); DRDO award for Performance Excellence as team member . Award conferred by Raksha Mantri of India (2016); Commendation by PRESIDENT REPUBLIC OF INDIA on Successful Test-Firing of Medium Range Surface to Air Missile (MRSAM) (2016); Outstanding Teamwork Award for Developing MMIC Technology” (MMICs) in 2001 by Scientific Advisor to RAKSHA MANTRI. (2001) SCOPE Eminence Award for Institutional Excellence (2025) by the Hon’ble President of India; ELCINA Defennovation Award 2025 for R&D Excellence in Strategic Electronics; IETE Corporate Award 2024 for Electronic Instruments and Instrumentation; SCOPE Meritorious Award 2024 for Technology Development & Innovation by the Hon’ble Vice President of India; Multiple National & International Quality Awards (NCQC, ICQCC, CCQC) and Rajbhasha Awards Fellow of IETE; Life member of ISSS, SAQR, and INS; Chairman, SETS (Society for Electronic Transactions and Security); Member of Promotional Boards of Scientists Authored numerous research papers published in reputed national and international journals and conferences, many indexed in SCI and Scopus , with recognized H-Index impact.; Strong proponent of Atmanirbhar Bharat , actively advancing indigenous technology development and manufacturing excellence.; Research areas include RF MEMS-based phase shifters , MMICs and aerospace-grade electronics qualification .

content: Shri P. Krishna Kumar, ITS (1993) Chief Vigilance Officer Shri P. Krishna Kumar , a 1992 batch officer of the Indian Telecom Service (ITS), joined Electronics Corporation of India Limited (ECIL) as Chief Vigilance Officer (CVO) on 26th November 2022. He holds a B.Tech from the College of Engineering, Osmania University and an M.Tech from IIT Madras. He was selected for the PGPPM (Post Graduate Programme in Public Policy and Management) at IIM Bangalore and Syracuse University (USA), where he completed a thesis on 'Skill Development as a Tool to Eradicate Poverty'. He also earned an MBA from Osmania University and is currently pursuing a Ph.D. in Behavioural Change Management at the same institution. During stay in Department of Telecom, he provided STD facility to hundreds of rural telephone exchanges using optical fiber and digital microwave systems. He launched mobile services in the Srinagar Valley in 2003, after obtaining all necessary permissions from the Army and law enforcement agencies. He played a key role in deploying a mobile service network with a capacity of 9.6 lakh during the year 2004 and 2008. As a Commercial Officer in BSNL, he introduced several competitive tariffs and plans, getting lakhs of customers and huge revenue for the company. Earlier, he held the position of Director (Security) and Sr. DDG, AP LSA, Department of Telecom, Hyderabad, where he was responsible for Lawful Interception and Cyber Security of telecom and internet networks. Over his 30-year career, he has held various key positions within the Department of Telecommunications, BSNL, Department of Pharmaceuticals, etc. Prior to his appointment at ECIL, he served as Director (Pharmaceuticals) in the Department of Pharmaceuticals on a Central Staffing Scheme deputation, starting in August 2020. While working as Director, DoP, he was responsible for the administration of 7 NIPERs and the PMBJP scheme etc. He also served as Director and Chief Vigilance Officer (CVO) at Hindustan Antibiotics Limited (HAL), Pune and Indian Rare Earths Limited (IREL), Mumbai. title: Electronics Manufacturing Services Division (EMSD) | ECIL | DAE | India
content: Empowering national and strategic programs through trusted, innovative, and secure electronic manufacturing. EMSD specializes in the mass production of strategic electronic systems and high-density PCB assemblies. Located on a 55-acre campus with 10,000 sq. m of advanced facilities, EMSD integrates automation, precision assembly, and testing to deliver secure, high-quality, and time-bound manufacturing. For over two decades, EMSD has been a pillar of India’s electoral infrastructure, producing over 3 million Electronic Voting Machines (EVMs) for the Election Commission of India and State Election Commissions. Known for their simplicity, reliability, and durability, these EVMs have revolutionized the nation’s voting process. Equipped with state-of-the-art automation and precision inspection systems, EMSD stands as a preferred partner for organizations Manufactured 250,000 PCB assemblies (SMT and through-hole) for single-phase static electronic energy meters supplied to electricity boards. Supplies complex multilayer PCB assemblies for NPCIL, PFBR, Defence and other strategic projects, meeting stringent stage-wise quality checks including optical and X-ray inspections for 100% compliance . End-to-end conversion of design to product - component procurement (electronic, mechanical, electromechanical, plastics), PCB population, system integration, ATP-based testing and delivery. Precision Manufacturing, Proven Performance, Scalable Electronics Services You Can Rely On. Securing Democracy Through Trusted Technical Support - Powering Free and Fair Elections Every Step of the Way Promoting public participation and trust in democratic processes through broad societal engagement. Beyond public elections, EMSD leverages its expertise to conduct elections for clubs, associations, unions, and committees, ensuring optimal utilization and additional revenue generation. Enhancing design, security, and usability. Developing systems for faster assembly and inspection. Leveraging manufacturing data for process optimization and informed decision-making. Building efficient, high-volume production systems. Exploring export potential for EVMs and accessories. Electronics Manufacturing Services Division (EMSD), Cherlapalli, ECIL Post, Hyderabad -500062. 040 - 29808937, 27260037, 27260655 Electronics Manufacturing Services Division (EMSD) has the state of art equipment for carrying out assembly of components on to PCBs of EVMs, VVAPTs, M7 Radios, Energy Meters and Telecom products etc. which are required to be produced in large numbers. EMSD today is fully automatic and comparable to any of the best manufacturing facilities in the country. Many of the assembly capabilities have been augmented since the start of the New Assembly Facility at EMSD built on an area of 5000 Square meters. These are:- SMT (surface mount technology) pick-and-place machines or P&Ps, are robotic machines which are used to place surface-mount devices (SMDs) onto a printed circuit board (PCB). They are used for high speed placement rate, high precision placing of broad range of electronic components, like capacitors, resistors, integrated circuits onto the PCBs with integrated digital vision. In Surface Mount Assembly, Solder Paste Printing is the most critical process for product quality perspective. Solder Paste printing process is the common way of applying solder paste onto a PCB, which is performed by printing solder paste through apertures in a stencil. It is very Important of surface mount Assembly process and also known as screen Printing. The reason for applying solder paste is to be able to receive electrical and mechanical connection of components to the PCB after component assembly and reflow soldering. Solder Paste Inspection is mainly done to check the solder paste deposits in the PCB assembly process. With the help of SPI, we can reduce the defects related to soldering by a considerable amount. Advanced equipment are used for precise inspection of the Solder Paste applied on PCBs. Angle cameras are used to take 3D pictures, which are very helpful in measuring the alignment and volume of the solder paste. Reflow soldering is a process in which a solder paste is used to attach one or thousands of electrical components to their contact pads, in which the entire assembly is subjected to controlled heat. The solder paste reflows in a molten state, creating permanent solder joints. AOI, automatic optical inspection systems use visual methods to monitor printed circuit boards for defects. They are able to detect a variety of surface feature defects such as scratches and stains as well as the more familiar defects such as short circuits, excess and dry solder. They can also detect incorrect components, missing components and incorrectly placed components. As such they are able to perform all the visual checks performed previously by manual operators and far more swiftly and accurately. Dry Thermal Storage Cabinets are used for drying and storage of multi-layer PCBs before and after mounting, including dual side boards awaiting second side reflow. MSD Components are also stored in Dry Cabinets. Trace moisture causes failure of components and PCBs during high temperature reflow process. When absorbed moisture rapidly expand from high temperatures, common internal component damages and failures such as micro-cracking, blistering, popcorn effects will occur in moisture sensitive devices, packages and components. Dry cabinets provide ultra-low humidity storage environment and handling for MSDs and PCBs. Selective soldering is the process of selectively soldering components to printed circuit boards that could be damaged by the heat of a reflow oven or wave soldering. Selectively soldered are usually surrounded by parts that have been previously soldered in a surface-mount reflow process and the selective-solder process must be sufficiently precise to avoid damaging them. Wave soldering is a bulk soldering process used in the assembly of printed circuit boards. The circuit board is passed over a pan of molten solder in which a pump produces an upwelling of solder that looks like a standing wave. As the circuit board makes contact with this wave, the components become soldered to the board. The objective of the PCB cleaning process is to remove all kind of solder residues to avoid any high level of failures that can occur in the early life period of the product. To ensure the reliability of bonding and coating processes, it is of utmost importance to clean the assemblies. Fully automatic cleaning machine Provides superb cleaning for high volume of electronic assemblies. Flying Probe in circuit Tester(FPT) is used for testing low to mid volume production, prototypes, and boards. FPT uses four flying probes, which may be moved based on software instructions. The flying probes are electro-mechanically controlled to access components on PCB assemblies. The probes are moved around the board under test using an automatically operated two-axis system, and one or more test probes contact components of the board or test points on the PCBs. title: Antenna Products & SATCOM Division (AP&SD) | ECIL | DAE | India
content: ECIL played a pioneering role in supporting the ambitious programs of ISRO. ECIL's Antenna Products & SATCOM Divsion has its lineage that dates back to 1968, where ARVI Satellite Communication(ASCOM) group was constituted by drawing experts from various organizations to execute the design, developement, manufacturing, installation, testing & commissioning of the country's first INTELSAT Class-A Earth Station Antenna at ARVI, Pune for providing the gateway for overseas communications for the traffic originating around Mumbai region. ASCOM group has designed the 97ft Earth Station Antenna with a king post Elevation over Azimuth pedestal, servo system and antenna control unit. The station was installed and commissioned in 1968. The Feed was imported. The control and servo system was developed by BARC. After the completion of the above project, Microwave Antenna System Engineers Group{MASEG(ISRO)} was formed to further the R&D activities on Microwave and Satellite earth station antennas for providing communication facilities in the country. The MASEG group got merged with ECIL in 1972 and Antenna Products Divsion was formed in ECIL with the aim to take up commercial production of Microwave and Earth station antennas. In 1975, ECIL delivered another 97ft Earth Station Antenna with king post pedestal (similar to ARVI Antenna) at Lachhiwala in Dehradun for providing the International gateway to the traffic originating from Delhi region. The expertise gained during the execution of above two projects has firmed up the knowledge base at ECIL to take up designa and production of various types of communication antennas.

title: Profile of Air Marshal Praveen Keshav Vohra, UYSM, AVSM, VM, DCIDS (PP & FD) | ECIL | DAE | India
tags: Profile of Air Marshal Praveen Keshav Vohra, UYSM, AVSM, VM, DCIDS (PP & FD)
content: Air Marshal Praveen Keshav Vohra UYSM, AVSM, VM, DCIDS (PP & FD) Air Marshal Praveen Keshav Vohra, UYSM, AVSM, VM was commissioned into the Fighter Stream of the Indian Air Force on 19 Dec 1987. He is an alumnus of National Defence Academy, Khadakwasala. The Air Officer has rich experience of operational flying and has flown over 3400 hours on various aircraft which include MiG-29, all variants of the MiG-21 and the SU-30 MKI. He is a graduate of the Defence Services Staff College, Wellington and Centre of Defence and Strategic Studies, Australia. The Air Officer commanded No 47 Sqn. ‘The Black Archers’. He has been the Air Officer Commanding of Air Force Station Halwara and Air Officer Commanding Jammu Kashmir & Ladakh. His key appointments at Air HQ (VB) and Command HQ, include Director at Directorate of Personnel Officers, Air Commodore (Operations & Strategy), Air Assistant to the Chief of the Air Staff, Assistant Chief of the Air Staff Operations, Senior Air Staff Officer (Western Air Command). In addition to being a Cat ‘A’ Qualified Flying Instructor, he is a founder member of the IAF’s formation aerobatic team the ‘Suryakirans’. He has been the Commodore Commandant of No. 47 Sqn. Prior to taking over as Deputy Chief of Integrated Defence Staff (PP & FD), he was the Commandant, Air Force Academy. In recognition for his meritorious services he was awarded ‘Vayu Sena Medal’ in 2007, ‘Ati Vishisht Seva Medal’ in 2017 and ‘Uttam Yudh Seva Medal’ in 2025 for his role in ‘Op Sindoor’ by the President of India. He is married to Mrs Navita Arjun Vohra, an Architect and an avid Painter. They are blessed with a son who is a lawyer and an actor.
